## Additions from c2-resume (D020-D024)
Classification key: MP = Manager policy | LP = lab-provider behaviour | CC = reusable CC operation | CMP = component | AM = agent methodology. Anything not listed as demonstrated is "not demonstrated".

Orchestrator policy: invalid UTF-8 in GENERATED text is flagged, not failed (att-2 st_prose_n18 flagged invalid_utf8 and still scored, D022); a flagged output is never silently clean. Limits: literal argument paths only, no indirect dependencies, no check after verification. 48 CPU-only tests; not run against a live job.
3. **A rerun is a new attempt, never a relabel** (MP). Event: D020 was completed as job-8df3c7bb27 att-2; att-1 stays `interrupted` with its partial output. Same rule as earlier retry-as-new (job-9252e2d8bf att-2).
4. **Memory-budget guarantee taxonomy** (MP). Classes: none | cooperative-intercept | cgroup-host | hard. The gpu_budget LD_PRELOAD shim is cooperative-intercept only: bypassable via VMM pool (cuMemCreate), static cudart, cuGetProcAddress, other processes (D021). With NO_VMM it counted weights 778.7 + KV 192 + compute 108 MiB (peak 1078.9) vs ~1388 MiB nvidia-smi delta, ~310 MiB uncounted (D023). Cap 900 + forced -ngl 99: KV denied, clean abort rc=1 (enforcement works on intercepted paths). Rules: report shim peak AND nvidia-smi delta, declare n_ctx, place experts explicitly (auto-fit under the virtual budget placed 155 MiB, D023). Hard device-memory limit: not demonstrated. cgroup-host class: container memory limits exist (job-6e6b2d39b8) but are not a GPU guarantee.
5. **Image identity: four different digests** (CC+MP). Docker reported ID (`image inspect .Id`), config digest, manifest digest, index digest. Under the containerd store `.Id` is the INDEX digest (D016). Buildx metadata there has only `containerimage.digest` (= index) and no `config.digest`, so T-N code failed novmm-1 at inspect_image (D023); T-N2 derives config digest from the saved archive and cross-checks metadata when present. Rule: record the config digest for admission/observation, keep a separate `run_ref` for execution, never treat an index digest as a config ID. Receiving a repo@digest of a local-only image: rejected in a prior probe (per T-N2 assignment); run_ref field in shot-2/novmm-3 records is the evidence of the current approach, not yet shown for novmm-2/shot-1 reruns.

Rule: every CC that parses another tool's output needs at least one saved real-record fixture (e.g. cc/build_engine/fixtures/buildx-metadata-containerd-real.json) before acceptance. # D008 — Decode profile of Granite BF16 on llama.cpp (build 11723) and first screens
Evidence: artifacts/profiles/tg128.nsys-rep (graph-level), tg128_node.nsys-rep (node-level), *_kern_sum.csv, lab/jobs/job-faead0556b (screen1).
- Graph-level trace (less perturbing): per-token GPU graph exec median 1580 us, inter-graph gap median 170 us => ~90% GPU execution, ~10% host gap. Unprofiled decode 599 t/s (A/A spread 0.5-2%).
- Node-level trace: ~487 kernels/token; ~71% of kernel time in 3 BF16 matmul kernels (mul_mat_vec_f bf16 x2, mul_mat_f bf16). BUT node-level tracing inflated the inter-token gap to ~507 us and graph-launch to ~367 us: PROFILER PERTURBATION. First reading (25% host gap) was wrong; corrected by comparing with graph-level trace. Lesson for methodology CC: cross-check any profiler-derived overhead number against a lower-perturbation trace and unprofiled wall time.
- Per-token host work seen between graphs: 196,620 B D2H (logits 49155 x f32), ~10 tiny H2D copies + syncs (~70 us), graph launch.
- Screen1 (runtime env, n=6 attempts, counterbalanced ABAB): ctrl 599.1 t/s; GGML_CUDA_GRAPH_OPT=1 595.8 (-0.55%, not supported); GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1 574.1 (-4.2%, graphs help).
- Next hypotheses: H-quant (representation: Q8_0, Q4_K_M, labelled), H-bw (BF16 matvec kernels reach only part of DRAM bandwidth: needs ncu), H-gap (<=10% ceiling for host-gap work), H-fuse (fewer small kernels).
# D011 — Bandwidth screen (ncu) and Q8_0 decode profile; engine candidate selected
Evidence: artifacts/profiles/tg_matmul_ncu.{ncu-rep,csv} (ncu 2025.1.1, SYS_ADMIN, profiling-only timings, NOT inference speed); q8_tg128_{node,graph}.{nsys-rep,sqlite}.
BF16 (D008): MoE expert matvec (grid 512x8, 16.8 MB, 25 us) = 75% DRAM peak (~665 GB/s, spec peak 896 GB/s is a published value, not measured here); attention projections (1-2 MB, 4-6 us) only 30-44% => latency-bound; mul_mat_f 63%. => BF16 kernel-level headroom small (<~7% overall); weight bytes are the lever (confirmed by Q8_0 +32% decode, D009).
Q8_0 decode: graph exec median 1171 us + gap 178 us => 741 tok/s (profiled graph-level; unprofiled screen 794). 633 kernels/token (vs 487 BF16): +146 quantize_q8_1/token = 14.4% of kernel time, avg 1.6 us each.
Kernel order in a layer shows 3 separate quantize_q8_1 of the same normed activation before the q, k, v matvecs (artifacts/profiles/q8_tg128_node.sqlite).
Selected engine candidate C1 (H-fuse-q8): reuse one q8_1 quantization of an activation across consecutive consumers. Prediction: remove ~2 quantize launches/layer (~48/token, ~53 us of 1171) => ~3-4.5% decode. Success criterion (frozen before assessment): >= +2% decode on matched counterbalanced A/B (A/A bound 0.5-2%), outputs bit-identical (mean KLD 0, top-1 100% vs unpatched Q8_0), no PPL change. If <2% or non-identical => rejected, reported as such.
Not chosen now: BF16 kernel tuning (<=7% ceiling), graph-opt env (rejected D008), fusing norm+quantize (larger change, defer).

# T-R: Granite hot GPU / cold CPU engine candidate
Private experimental fork of llama.cpp `31288c9c66e59377f7788d920678a565bb89dd37`.
Patch SHA256: `1063ac102a14bff798d56b5bf292d21455f3f4c847f0e2043d98d58126bd1efb`.
The engine patch is `cc/hybrid_split/hybrid-split.patch`; the applied tree and all
execution evidence are under `artifacts/codexR/`. `ref/` was not modified.
No network, Docker, CUDA compilation, or GPU execution was used by this worker.
All local builds used `GGML_CUDA=OFF` and at most `-j4`; inference used four threads.
**CPU result:** original mixE4K versus each of the n18/n12/n6 matched split files:
64/64 greedy tokens identical, maximum absolute logit difference **0**, RMS logit
difference **0**. This establishes CPU numerical correctness for this prompt,
not a GPU speedup or mixed-device numerical equivalence.
## Format and integration conditions
Source: `/home/muk/models/campaign/gguf/granite-3.1-1b-a400m-instruct-mixE4K.gguf`,
SHA256 `2e520c4a7b15ce292cc88e92fef00fb99da276dc5d6fc8e8f832b8525f8565a6`.
It is `granitemoe`, 24 layers, 32 experts, top-8, embedding 1024, FFN 512.
Actual GGML dimensions (fastest dimension first) and types are:
| Tensor in each `blk.L` | GGML shape | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ffn_gate_inp.weight` | `[1024,32]` | F32 |
| `ffn_gate_exps.weight` | `[1024,512,32]` | Q4_K |
| `ffn_up_exps.weight` | `[1024,512,32]` | Q4_K |
| `ffn_down_exps.weight` | `[512,1024,32]` | Q4_K |
Each expert in each projection is 294,912 packed bytes. A complete expert across
three projections is 884,736 bytes (0.84375 MiB).
`split_gguf.py` uses only the pinned `ref/llama.cpp/gguf-py` and installed NumPy.
It takes the `make_hot_set.py` text format: comments plus `layer expert` rows.
Within each layer it sorts the hot original IDs, appends the remaining original
IDs, permutes the F32 router rows consistently, and copies packed expert blocks
without dequantization or requantization. It replaces each expert tensor with:
- `<original-name>.hot`: `[ne0,ne1,H+1]`, with H real hot experts followed by one
  all-zero null expert in the same packed type.
- `<original-name>.cold`: `[ne0,ne1,32-H]`, holding the remaining real experts.
- `blk.L.ffn_expert_ids.ids_hot`: I32 `[1,32]`, original ID to hot slot or H.
- `blk.L.ffn_expert_ids.ids_cold`: I32 `[1,32]`, original ID to cold slot or -1.
- `blk.L.ffn_expert_ids.ids_router`: I32 `[32]`, original ID to permuted router row.
The three ID tensors are per layer, not per expert projection. Metadata records
`hybrid_split.version=1`, source/hot-set SHA256 values, hot counts and a flattened
new-index-to-original-index permutation. Other metadata and tensors are copied.
Only little-endian `granitemoe` with 32 experts is accepted. The transform supports
F32/F16/Q4_K/Q8_0 expert banks with F32 routers; the real validation used Q4_K.
Each layer must have 0..31 hot experts; all-hot layers are rejected because GGUF
zero-sized cold banks are unsupported. Unknown expert/router companion tensors,
duplicate/out-of-range hot entries, existing outputs and already split inputs
are rejected. Production CLI GGUF output paths are restricted to
`artifacts/codexR/models/`; pytest temporary GGUFs are also placed there.
The loader recognizes optional split banks only for Granite MoE. Existing
expert pointers own the hot banks; extra layer pointers hold cold banks and ID
maps. All use existing model buffer contexts and normal tensor ownership. There
are no new backend allocations, callbacks, placement APIs or CUDA kernels.
Missing/partial banks, inconsistent shapes and non-I32 maps fail loading. Map
contents are checked for a bijective router permutation and consistent local
IDs when the graph is built, after weights are loaded.
Required runtime flags are:
```text
-ngl 99 -ot '\.cold$=CPU' --no-op-offload --no-repack --no-warmup
```
`-ot` is the existing tensor buffer override. `--no-op-offload` is necessary:
the scheduler can otherwise move CPU weight operations to CUDA during prefill.
The split graph explicitly rejects op offload. `--no-repack` ensures plain CPU
buffers reach the modified generic CPU kernel; optimized repacked CPU buffers
have separate MUL_MAT_ID implementations. Cold non-host buffers are rejected.
Do not combine split models with `--moe-cache-mib`, LoRA, Hadamard transforms,
expert biases/scales, post-expert normalization, or other activation functions;
the split branch rejects these combinations. No KV or attention code is changed.

Routing uses the existing router, softmax, top-k, weight normalization and scaling.
After router matmul, transpose/contiguous/GET_ROWS/transpose/contiguous restores
logits to the **original** expert order before softmax and top-k. This preserves
both floating-point reduction order and original-ID tie-breaking despite the
on-disk permutation. It uses existing operations on the GPU, not an I32 REPEAT
(which this CUDA backend does not support). Two further existing I32 GET_ROWS
operations map flattened selected IDs into the hot and cold partitions.
CPU MUL_MAT_ID explicitly zeros each negative-ID destination column and omits it
from the per-expert work lists. Positive bounds use `GGML_ASSERT`, so Release
builds still reject positive out-of-range IDs. Skips perform no expert dot
products or expert-weight accesses. ID scanning, output zeroing, activation
conversion and dense activation work still have a fixed top-8 overhead; total
latency is not claimed to be strictly proportional to the number of cold IDs.
The negative-ID convention is **CPU-only**, and requires plain CPU buffers.
CUDA always receives in-range hot IDs.
The null expert has exactly zero gate, up and down weights. Its unweighted
contribution is zero; original routing weights are applied **once** after adding
hot/cold slot outputs. No separate zero weight mask is needed. Normalization
and expert scaling remain in the shared original code, ahead of this branch.
Slot outputs are reduced in the original selected-slot order.

worker**. They require the orchestrator's Docker/CUDA environment and cached,
identified base images. Build CC currently uses `--parallel 10` internally;

`-j4`. Build CC's runtime base digest resolution must succeed locally.
```bash

  --tag campaign/llamacpp:hybrid-split-r \
  --out artifacts/codexR/cuda-build
```
Build CC fixes `LLAMA_BUILD_TESTS=OFF` and rejects overrides of that built-in key.
The patch's default-OFF `LLAMA_BUILD_HYBRID_SPLIT_TESTS` option exposes the tests
subdirectory for those explicit extra targets despite that fixed setting. This
configuration was compiled locally with CUDA OFF, including both test targets.
```bash
docker run --rm --network none --gpus all \
  campaign/llamacpp:hybrid-split-r /app/test-hybrid-split --backend CUDA0
docker run --rm --network none --gpus all \
  campaign/llamacpp:hybrid-split-r \
  /app/test-backend-ops -b CUDA0 -o GET_ROWS -p 'type=i32' -j 1
for ncpu in 18 12 6; do
  docker run --rm --network none --gpus all \
    -v "$PWD/artifacts/codexR/models:/models:ro" \
    -v "$PWD/artifacts/traces/in:/prompts:ro" \
    campaign/llamacpp:hybrid-split-r /app/llama-completion \
    -m "/models/granite-split-n${ncpu}.gguf" \
    -ngl 99 -ot '\.cold$=CPU' --no-op-offload --no-repack \
    --no-warmup -c 4096 -n 160 -t 4 -tb 4 --temp 0 --seed 1 \
    -f /prompts/chat.txt --no-display-prompt \
    > "artifacts/codexR/cuda-n${ncpu}.stdout" \
    2> "artifacts/codexR/cuda-n${ncpu}.stderr"

```
The focused CUDA command keeps negative IDs exclusively on its CPU cold backend,
checks the scheduler assignment, and checks hot/null computation on CUDA. It
covers F32 and Q4_K, one and 17 tokens, broadcast and per-slot activations, mixed,
all-hot and all-cold routing, nontrivial permutations, router restoration, and
NaN-poisoned reused skipped outputs. It does not add negative-ID CUDA support.
Use the existing campaign GPU monitor/budget shim to record memory and transfers
when benchmarking; the commands above alone do not establish equal GPU MiB.

cmake --build artifacts/codexR/repro-build \

artifacts/codexR/repro-build/bin/test-hybrid-split
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -q \
  cc/hybrid_split/test_split_gguf.py \
  --basetemp=artifacts/codexR/models/pytest-tmp \

c++ -std=c++17 -O2 cc/hybrid_split/compare_logits.cpp \

  -L artifacts/codexR/repro-build/bin \

lines: Question: at long context, how much GPU memory does KV quantization save on Granite mixE4K, at what quality and speed cost? KV/token f16 = 24 layers x 2 x 8 kv-heads x 64 x 2 B = 48 KiB -> 1.5 GiB at 32k ctx (> mixE4K weights 779 MiB).

Image: llamacpp-b0 (unpatched 31288c9c6). Tests lab/tests/kv1.json: decode/prefill at -c 32768 with the 1560-token prose prompt (-n 96) for KV f16/q8_0/q4_0 with -fa on, plus f16 -fa off control; 3 alternating rounds; PPL wikitext -c 4096 --chunks 6 per KV type.

Accept a KV type as "same accuracy" if PPL within +1% of f16 (-fa on) AND greedy text identical or (if not) KLD check pending; report GPU delta MiB (nvidia-smi), prefill & decode t/s medians. Classification: representation (KV) trade-off — not an engine code gain.

+- Quantized KV (q8_0, q4_0; -fa on) ABORTS at model load: ggml-impl.h:330 hash-set "fatal error" (SIGSEGV 139), in our b0 build AND the upstream ghcr full-cuda image at the same commit, with fit on or off, at 4k and 32k ctx -> engine defect in llama.cpp 31288c9c6 for this model/config, not our build. Delegated root cause: T-KVB. KV precision lever UNTESTED, not "rejected".

+- Flash attention alone (f16 KV, -c 32768, 1560-token prompt): GPU delta 2762 MiB (-fa on) vs 3746 MiB (-fa off) = -984 MiB; decode 627.2 vs 570.2 t/s (+10%), prefill 7001 vs 5865 t/s (+19%); text differs (96310158 vs f28de009; FA changes reduction order). PPL -c 4096 f16 FA 7.5385 (no non-FA PPL run -> quality equivalence of FA not measured here).

+Classification: memory-fit + speed observation for an existing engine option; factory rule candidate: "enable flash attention for long context (removes the O(ctx) KQ buffer)". 3 samples (gen), 1 (ppl).

# Assignment T-KVB (campaign c2-resume, x86-main; owner Claude Opus; worker Codex) — engine defect root cause

Use a backtrace (gdb if available, or -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo + backtrace print) to locate the caller. Check whether upstream later fixed it only if you can find evidence in-tree (no network).
Deliver: patch, artifacts/codexKVB/ROOTCAUSE.md (mechanism, why only quantized KV, why Granite?), CPU repro before/after logs, and the exact orchestrator command to build via Build CC (`--patch`) + verify on CUDA.
Allowed writes: cc/kv_quant_fix/**, artifacts/codexKVB/**. 60 min, no network, no Docker, -j4 max, nice. Final message: root cause in 3 sentences, patch sha256, evidence, open risks.
EOF
cat > assignments/T-PROF-split-vs-static.md <<'EOF'
# Assignment T-PROF (campaign c2-resume, x86-main; owner Claude Opus; worker Codex) — profile analysis for D030
Question: why is the hybrid expert split (cc/hybrid_split, decisions/D030) 16-32% SLOWER than static layer offload (--n-cpu-moe) at equal GPU MiB, with the deficit growing as more experts are hot?
Inputs (nsys 2024.6.2 graph-level traces, --sample=none --cpuctxsw=none, -t cuda,nvtx,osrt, --cuda-graph-trace=graph; same binary; chat prompt -n 160 decode): artifacts/x4-hs/prof/split-n12.sqlite and static-n12.sqlite (+ .nsys-rep). Note D008: graph-level traces perturb less; node-level not captured. Read decisions/D008, D011, D019, D030 and cc/hybrid_split/README.md (design: per-slot hot dispatch, router GET_ROWS reorder, CPU cold MUL_MAT_ID, 24 layers each with CPU work).
Do (Python sqlite3 only, light CPU): per decode token (segment by the per-token pattern, discard the first ~5 tokens as warmup): count of CUDA graph launches, kernel launches outside graphs, cudaStreamSynchronize/cudaMemcpy (by kind/size) calls and time, D2H/H2D bytes, GPU busy time, GPU idle gaps (count + total), and wall time per token; top kernels by total time for each; identify whether split runs ANY kernels inside CUDA graphs (graph reuse broken?). Produce a side-by-side table and attribute the per-token difference (split - static) into buckets: extra GPU kernels, extra syncs/transfers, CPU-side time while GPU idle, graph capture loss.
Then propose (do not implement) the 2-3 most promising redesigns with a predicted per-token saving each, grounded in the numbers (e.g. CUDA MUL_MAT_ID supporting negative/skip IDs to avoid per-slot dispatch; grouping cold work so only K layers touch the CPU; overlapping CPU cold compute with GPU hot compute via async copies).
Deliver artifacts/codexPROF/ANALYSIS.md + analyze_nsys.py (reusable tool: a profiling CC for "per-token decode breakdown from nsys sqlite") + its pytest on a tiny synthetic sqlite. Allowed writes: cc/nsys_decode/** (the tool), artifacts/codexPROF/**. 40 min, no GPU, no Docker, light CPU. Final message: the table, attribution, proposals, tool usage.
EOF
cat > assignments/T-PAP-placement-aware-precision.md <<'EOF'
# Assignment T-PAP (campaign c2-resume, x86-main; owner Claude Opus; worker Codex) — factory technique: placement-aware expert precision (+ imatrix)
Hypothesis (orchestrator): with `--n-cpu-moe K` (experts of the FIRST K layers on CPU), the CPU part is DRAM-bandwidth bound (~26 GB/s on this Ryzen 7 3700X: 8 Q4_K experts x 0.84 MiB per layer per token in ~0.26 ms; D014/D022). Requantizing ONLY the CPU-resident layers' experts to fewer bits (Q3_K, Q2_K) should speed the CPU part ~proportionally to bytes and cut host RAM, while GPU layers keep Q4_K; quality loss is confined to K layers. D013: all-layer 3-bit experts KLD 0.135 (vs 0.040 at 4-bit), 2-bit collapses (0.77) — WITHOUT imatrix; imatrix calibration untried and likely helps low bits.
Tools: the upstream image ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp@sha256:395d01bb... has llama-quantize/llama-imatrix but you cannot run Docker. So build CPU-only llama-quantize + llama-imatrix from a scratch tree (artifacts/codexPAP/tree = git archive ref/llama.cpp 31288c9c6; -DGGML_CUDA=OFF; -j4; nice). Source model: ~/models/campaign/gguf/granite-3.1-1b-a400m-instruct-bf16.gguf (read-only). mixE4K recipe (decisions/D013): `llama-quantize --tensor-type 'ffn_.*_exps=q4_K' bf16 out Q8_0`.
Do: (1) imatrix: compute with llama-imatrix on CPU (-t 6) over wikitext-2 TRAIN text (~/models/campaign/data/wikitext/wikitext-2-raw/wiki.train.raw; bounded: e.g. --chunks 100 -c 512) -> artifacts/codexPAP/models/granite-wtrain.imatrix (record chunks, sha). Evaluation will use wiki.test -> disjoint. (2) Produce GGUFs into artifacts/codexPAP/models/ (llama-quantize supports per-tensor regex --tensor-type; verify exact syntax in-tree): for K in {12, 18, 24}: pap{K}_q3 (blk 0..K-1 experts q3_K, other experts q4_K, rest Q8_0), pap{K}_q2 (q2_K), each WITH imatrix, plus pap24_q3_noimat (= mixE3K-equivalent control w/o imatrix) and mix4_imat (all experts q4_K with imatrix) control. Record file sizes, per-layer types (verify by reading tensors with gguf-py), sha256. (3) Write lab tests JSON lab-tests-pap.json (schema: lab/tests/match1.json + mem2.json kl_q8 for KLD: `llama-perplexity -c 512 --chunks 20 -ngl 99 --kl-divergence-base /out/bf16.kl --kl-divergence` with docker_args mount of artifacts/kl) covering: decode at matching --n-cpu-moe K for each pap{K} AND the mixE4K baseline at same K; KLD for every model; files must be referenced by basename (orchestrator will place them in one model dir). (4) Optional cheap CPU sanity: KLD on CPU for pap12_q3 only if bf16.kl compatible (else skip).
Deliver cc/pap/{make_pap.sh (reproducible recipe), README.md (technique, integration conditions: llama.cpp --n-cpu-moe offloads first K layers — verify in source and cite line; types per layer; imatrix provenance; claims allowed)}, artifacts/codexPAP/{models/*, MANIFEST.json, lab-tests-pap.json}. Allowed writes: cc/pap/**, artifacts/codexPAP/**. 75 min, no Docker, no network, -j4, nice. Checkpoint at 50 min. Final message: files + sizes, imatrix provenance, exact tests, gaps.

# D031 — Why the hybrid split loses on Granite (nsys, T-PROF) and the proxy-scale bias it reveals
Evidence: artifacts/codexPROF/ANALYSIS.md, cc/nsys_decode/analyze_nsys.py (new profiling CC), artifacts/x4-hs/prof/{split,static}-n12.sqlite (graph-level, same binary, 154 decode tokens after 5 warmup).
Per token: static n12 5.35 ms (13 graph launches, 110 syncs, GPU busy 1.06 ms = GPU idle ~80%); split n12 7.38 ms (25 graph launches, 194 syncs, GPU busy 2.55 ms). Extra 2.03 ms = 1.45 ms extra GPU graph work (per-slot hot dispatch: 1535 vs 583 kernels in first decode) + 0.37 ms exposed sync/transfers + 0.21 ms host. CUDA graphs ARE reused (no capture loss).
Interpretation (orchestrator): at batch 1 on this host, decode is dominated by per-layer CPU<->GPU handoff latency, not by expert bytes or GPU compute. The split computes FEWER CPU experts per token (~52 vs 96 at ~73% hot coverage) yet is slower because it pays the handoff in 24 layers instead of 12. T-PROF's best redesign (batched CUDA dispatch with skip IDs, -0.7..-1.1 ms) would only reach ~parity with static.
Transferability (key factory lesson): Granite experts are 0.84 MiB; the target (~500 GB MoE) has experts ~10-50x larger, so per-layer fixed costs amortize and expert-granular placement (hot GPU / cold CPU, Strata-style) should regain its advantage. Granite-only results systematically favour layer-granular placement. => The factory needs a second proxy that genuinely exceeds VRAM with larger experts before deciding placement granularity; Granite results on placement are labelled "small-expert regime".
Methodology rule: report per-layer fixed cost (handoff latency) alongside per-expert cost; predict crossover expert size = fixed_cost / per_byte_cost before choosing granularity.
EOF

# Memory, quality and speed report

Run from any working directory (Python standard library only):

```sh
python /home/muk/projects/siminfeng/campaign/cc/memory_pareto/pareto.py
python cc/memory_pareto/pareto.py experiments/memory/configs.csv --budget-mib 700
```

The script prints a Markdown table sorted by ascending GPU MiB (unknown memory last), followed by a terminal ASCII scatter of GPU MiB versus KLD. It writes `pareto.md` and `pareto.json` beside the script by default. `--output-dir artifacts/codexI` selects another assignment-permitted destination. Reports are overwritten on reruns. Nothing is written to the input paths. No network, Docker, or third-party runtime packages are used.

## Inputs

The primary input is `experiments/memory/configs.csv`, resolved relative to the campaign root, with these required headers:

```csv
config,desc,class,gpu_mib,host_mib,tg_ts,pp_ts,kld,top1_pct,ppl_ratio,notes
```

`class` must be `transferable`, `discrete-only`, or `mixed`. Supply the orchestrator's classifications; the script does not validate scientific transferability. Memory is MiB; TG and PP are tokens per second. KLD is smaller-is-better. Top1 is a percentage; PPL ratio is supplied relative to the experiment's stated reference. Neither is converted into KLD. Empty cells, NA, N/A, null, none, NaN and nonfinite numbers become unavailable, never zero. Invalid numbers, negative values, invalid classes, and percentages above 100 are errors. Zero is valid. Notes should identify workloads, hardware, model, measurement method and quality reference. Rows are individual observations; repeated names or exact metric ties are preserved.

If the default CSV is absent, the script reads `lab/jobs/*/att-*/result.json`, the corresponding `job.json` (`spec.model`), and `lab/tests/*.json` (test-specific `model_file`, args and env). `--lab-root` overrides this fallback root. An explicitly supplied CSV path that is absent is an error; an invalid or empty existing CSV never triggers fallback.

Fallback accepts completed attempts and successful, nonpartial tests only. It emits a separate row per benchmark sample record or quality test; it never joins observations across tests, attempts, models or workloads. GPU MiB means `mem.gpu_peak_mib`, **not** baseline-subtracted delta; host MiB means `host_cgroup_peak_mib`. TG requires zero prompt tokens and positive generated tokens; PP requires zero generated tokens and positive prompt tokens. Combined PP+TG samples supply neither speed objective. `avg_ts` supplies speed; repeated `samples_ts` are not independently analyzed. Raw PPL and its stderr are recorded in notes, but no PPL ratio or KLD is invented. Fallback classification is explicitly `unclassified`, so these rows cannot support transferable claims. Job/test/sample identifiers and source result paths are retained. Attempts are not averaged or deduplicated.

## Frontier and budget
# Campaign c1 — start here (wrap-up snapshot, 2026-11-09)
Goal (user, latest): methodology + tools for fitting a very large MoE (~500 GB weights -> 128 GB unified memory + 4 TB SSD) at similar accuracy and acceptable tokens/s. Proxy: ibm-granite/granite-3.1-1b-a400m-instruct on llama.cpp (commit 31288c9c6), RTX 5070 Ti (discrete). Every result is labelled transferable / discrete-only / prediction (D012).

## What is here
- `decisions/D001..D020` — chronological decisions with evidence (read D012-D020 first).
- `LAB-FEASIBILITY.md`, `MANAGER-DESIGN.md`, `cc-inventory.csv` — Lab Manager findings and the CC inventory (observed vs inferred).
- `bin/` — `run_op` (recorded commands), `lab` (image/job/attempt/cancel/reconcile/register/image-load/chaos), `perf_summary`, `index_evidence`, `cost_report`, `cuda_compile_check`.
- `cc/` — Build CC (`build_engine`), `engine_handoff`, `routing_trace` (patch + replay), `memory_pareto`, `hybrid_expert` (Opus harness), `q8_reuse` (UNTESTED speed patch), `gpu_budget` (memory-restriction shim, may be incomplete), tests (`pytest` in each dir).
- `evidence/*.jsonl` — raw per-agent streams (intent/started/outcome); `index/ops.jsonl` merged; `lab/jobs/*` job/attempt state + results; `experiments/` summaries; `claims/paper-claims.md` (15 source-supported claims, none tested yet).
Not committed (reproducible/bulky): llama.cpp clone (`ref/`), image archives, nsys/ncu reports, base logits, traces (regenerate with the lab tests), Codex scratch trees. Models live in `~/models/campaign` (Granite pin 0da7a48b; GGUFs bf16/Q8_0/Q4_K_M/mixE4K/3K/2K).

## Findings to trust (with caveats in the D-notes)
1. Experts are 90.4% of weight bytes; mixed precision (experts Q4_K, rest Q8_0) halves Q4_K_M's quality loss at equal memory (D013).
2. Static layer offload (`--n-cpu-moe`) cuts GPU MiB linearly but decode collapses (discrete-only, D014). Page-cache-as-expert-cache has a sharp cliff when RAM < working set (D015, contaminated by concurrent compiles).
3. Granite routing skew is real vs a uniform control (D017), mild, weaker pooled across workloads.
4. Hybrid hit/miss dispatch is bitwise-exact; the serial cost model holds (33 us/miss); perfect-overlap upper bound NOT supported (D019).
5. Engine-native `--moe-cache-mib` (LRU, upload-on-miss) is slower than no cache until ~60% coverage (job-d50c052f94). The matched static-offload comparison in the same tool did not finish (D020) — rerun `lab/tests/static1.json`.
6. Build CC: failures recorded (3 failed attempts), ccache makes patched rebuilds ~10-20 s; image identity bug found by independent observation (D016); real handoff `accepted` for the corrected record (experiments in `cc/engine_handoff/example-real5`).
7. Lab core bugs found by testing recovery per phase (D006, D020); duplicate delivery, sandbox kill, retry-as-new-attempt, stale/conflicting result rejection all demonstrated (LAB-FEASIBILITY.md, MANAGER-DESIGN.md).

Hard GPU-memory restriction shim (T-L) not compiled/tested by me; Strata concepts not yet applied end-to-end (only studied + CPU tests, and the single-layer harness); static hot-set expert placement (managed-memory idea, D018) not started; no end-to-end speed/memory result beats the baselines in a way I would call an engine win; q8_reuse patch not compiled; Opus/Codex outputs only partly reviewed; Claude-side token cost not captured.

# D035 — Placement-aware precision (PAP) + imatrix: results (protocol D032-A), job job-3d2fbbd061 (48/48 clean)
Conditions: llamacpp-b0, chat -n 160 -c 4096, 3 alternating rounds; host monitor: no compiler, BUT the 18.6 GB proxy-2 download ran throughout (dl=3) and round 3 was slower for several configs -> decode spread 10-15% within a config (vs 1-3% in D022/D029). Speed conclusions are therefore PROVISIONAL.
QUALITY (deterministic, 20x512 wikitext-test vs bf16 logits; solid):
  mixE4K KLD 0.040 top1 90.5 | mix4_imat (same types/bytes, imatrix from wikitext TRAIN) 0.027 / 91.9 (-33% KLD, free) |
  pap12_q3 0.073 / 87.3 | pap18_q3 0.086 / 85.8 | pap24_q3 0.117 / 83.6 vs pap24_q3_noimat 0.135 / 81.8 (imatrix -13%) |
  pap12_q2 0.193 | pap18_q2 0.258 | pap24_q2 0.359 (2-bit experts unacceptable even with imatrix and only in CPU layers).
SPEED (median decode t/s, same K vs mixE4K): pap12_q3 214.9 vs 195.7 (+9.8%), pap18_q3 +5.5%, pap24_q3 +8.7%, q2 variants +14..19%; mix4_imat vs mixE4K -3..+4% (identical bytes => file-level noise floor in this job ~±5%).
GPU MiB unchanged (PAP only touches CPU-resident layers); host cgroup peak unchanged (weights are mmap page cache, not charged) — PAP's memory effect is on file/page-cache size: pap12_q3 738 MB vs mixE4K 816 MB (-9.6%).
Verdict vs frozen rule (>= +5% AND KLD <= 0.08): pap12_q3 PROVISIONALLY ACCEPTED (speed needs a quiet-host 5-round rerun); all others rejected (quality). Imatrix: ACCEPTED as a factory default — same bytes, -33% KLD at 4-bit, -13% at 3-bit (calibration on wikitext-train; generalization beyond wikitext not tested).
Factory rules: (1) always quantize experts with an imatrix from a held-out calibration set; (2) lower-bit only for CPU-resident layers and only to 3-bit; (3) speed gain from PAP is bounded by the CPU share of decode time — it matters most where the CPU part dominates (big offloaded models).
EOF

# D036 — Engine components are separable at the binary level: swapping one backend .so carries the q8_reuse gain (E1)
Builds q8base-2 (unpatched) and q8reuse-2 (cc/q8_reuse patch) — separate Build CC runs, same commit/toolchain/base digests: of all shared libraries in /app, EXACTLY ONE differs: libggml-cuda.so.0.27.0 (base 14a7d2d8..., reuse f4011d9a...). libllama, libggml-base, libggml-cpu, libggml, libllama-common and all tool impl libs are byte-identical -> builds are reproducible and the q8_reuse component IS one backend library.

A backend-only component can be released and A/B-tested as a single .so against a fixed engine, if the ggml ABI version matches (0.27.0 here). Not shown: swaps across different ggml versions, or of components touching libllama (graph/loader), which need ABI/symbol checks (T-COMP).
EOF

# Assignment T-COMP (campaign c2-resume, x86-main; owner Claude Opus; worker Codex) — component versioning tools + composability experiment (E2)
Context: decisions/D036 — separately built images differ only in libggml-cuda.so when a CUDA-only patch is applied, and swapping that .so carries the gain. We now want engine components to be versioned units (by layer: model artifact, runtime config, backend .so, ggml core/scheduler, libllama graph/loader).

Deliver:
1. cc/components/patch_stack.py: for a list of patches: files/hunks touched per patch, map each touched file to an ENGINE LAYER (table: ggml/src/ggml-cuda/** -> backend-cuda (libggml-cuda.so); ggml/src/ggml-cpu/** -> backend-cpu; ggml/src/ggml-backend*.cpp, ggml.c, ggml-alloc* -> ggml-core (libggml-base.so); src/** -> libllama; common/** -> libllama-common; tools/** -> tool; CMake -> build), pairwise overlap, and an apply test in a scratch git-archive tree under artifacts/codexCOMP/: every permutation of the stack must apply cleanly and produce the IDENTICAL resulting tree hash (order-independence); report conflicts. Run it on [q8_reuse, kv_quant_fix] (the release stack) and [q8_reuse, kv_quant_fix, hybrid_split]. Write the combined release patch cc/components/release-stack-1.patch (q8_reuse+kv_quant_fix) with its sha256.
2. cc/components/abi_diff.py: compare two directories of shared libraries (ELF; reuse the pure-Python ELF reader in cc/build_engine from T-N3): per library sha256, SONAME, DT_NEEDED, exported dynamic symbols added/removed (and symbol version), so a backend .so swap can be declared ABI-compatible or not. Run on artifacts/x7-comp/base vs reuse (expect: only libggml-cuda differs; no exported-symbol change).
3. cc/components/COMPONENTS.md + components.schema.json: a minimal component manifest meaning (id, layer, kind source-patch|binary|artifact|runtime-flag, base commit, patch sha / file sha, binary outputs + ABI version (ggml 0.27.0), supported models/arch, prerequisites (e.g. flags), tests that qualify it, evidence decision ids, status). Fill manifests for q8_reuse, kv_quant_fix, imatrix-quantization (artifact recipe, D035), flash-attn (runtime flag, D028), kv-q8 (runtime flag requiring kv_quant_fix, D033), hybrid_split (rejected), static_hot (rejected), gpu_budget shim (infrastructure). If cc/factory/components.json exists (T-FAC in parallel), reconcile by READING it and writing a mapping note — do not edit cc/factory.
Tests: pytest for both tools (synthetic patches incl. a conflicting pair; synthetic ELF fixtures via T-N3 helpers).
Allowed writes: cc/components/**, artifacts/codexCOMP/**. 50 min, no Docker/GPU, CPU-only, nice. Final message: layer map of each patch, order-independence result + tree hashes, ABI diff result, release-stack sha256, gaps.
EOF
CAMPAIGN_ID=c1 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= nohup nice -n 15 bin/run_op --agent codex-COMP --parent X-c2 --task T-COMP --desc "codex exec assignments/T-COMP-component-versioning.md" -- codex exec --json -s workspace-write -C $PWD -o artifacts/codexCOMP/last-message.txt "Read and execute the assignment in $PWD/assignments/T-COMP-component-versioning.md exactly. # build_engine

Use this capability to turn a clean, identified local llama.cpp checkout and an optional Git patch into a local, runtime-only CUDA image and an evidence directory. It targets linux/amd64 and CUDA architecture 120 (RTX 5070 Ti). Model weights are supplied separately at runtime.

Requires Python 3.12+ (stdlib only), Git, Docker daemon access, and Docker Buildx/Bake. pytest is needed only for tests. No GPU is needed to compile or collect hashes. The builder installs Ubuntu build packages with apt; an actual build needs cached packages/base layers or repository/registry access. This implementation does not download source, patches, models, or web UI assets. The existing `campaign/cuda-tools:c1` image is not used as the builder because the required builder base is the digest-pinned NVIDIA devel image.

## Run

Run from the campaign directory. Give every attempt a new or empty output directory. For assignment T-N, keep outputs under `cc/build_engine/` or `artifacts/codexN/`. The CLI uses the Dockerfile and Bake recipe in `cc/build_engine/recipes/`; it does not modify or use the older recipes under `builds/llamacpp/`.

```bash
# Supply the real runtime image digest from trusted/local image evidence.
export BASE_RUNTIME='nvidia/cuda:12.8.1-runtime-ubuntu24.04@sha256:<64-hex-digest>'
python3 cc/build_engine/build_engine.py \
  --source ref/llama.cpp --commit 31288c9c6 \
  --tag campaign/llamacpp:c1 --out cc/build_engine/results/baseline
```

The placeholder must be replaced; it is not a working digest. If BASE_RUNTIME is unset, the CLI inspects the local runtime tag and selects its NVIDIA RepoDigest without pulling it. Missing local images or RepoDigests fail at `base_images`. BASE_DEVEL defaults to the devel digest already recorded in `artifacts/op-309e1f95c716/stdout`; override it with a full `nvidia/cuda:12.8.1-devel-ubuntu24.04@sha256:...` reference when needed. Both bases are validated and supplied as separate name and digest Dockerfile arguments. The CLI never builds from a floating base tag.

To add a patch, save a unified Git diff to a file and add `--patch path/to/change.patch`. Source HEAD must resolve to `--commit`; tracked changes and untracked files cause rejection. The source checkout remains read-only: Git optional locks are disabled, a `git archive` snapshot is extracted under the output directory, and `git apply --check` runs there before `git apply`. Git discovery stops before the enclosing campaign repository. Binary patches supported by Git are accepted. Submodules are rejected. Git archive honors committed export attributes; ignored and untracked files and `.git` are omitted. Docker ignore files in the staged snapshot are emptied to prevent omission of tracked source. Temporary staging is removed after either result. Keep the supplied patch and original commit for rebuilding; patch bytes are identified by SHA256 but are not retained as a separate output artifact.

The image contains only the seven requested tools in `/app`, their generated shared libraries and the OpenMP runtime, on top of the CUDA runtime base. It has no compiler, source checkout, or weights. Its entrypoint is cleared, so invoke tools by full path, for example `/app/llama-bench`. Release/shared CUDA compilation uses the flags in `build-record.json`; CPU-native tuning, tests, downloaded UI, and OpenSSL are disabled. `LLAMA_CURL=OFF` is passed as requested, although this checkout treats LLAMA_CURL as deprecated. Source and patch identity are recorded as image labels; binaries' built-in Git version may say `unknown` because `.git` is not staged.

## Engine variants and linkage

Use repeatable `--cmake-define KEY=VALUE` options. Keys must match `^[A-Z0-9_]+$`; values must be nonempty and contain only ASCII letters, digits, or `_./:+,@%=-`. Whitespace, shell metacharacters, empty values, duplicate keys (even with identical values), and all built-in keys are rejected before output creation. This also reserves the built-in compiler-launcher and executable-linker flags. Definitions are sorted by key, passed as the `CMAKE_DEFINES` build argument as space-separated `-DKEY=VALUE` words, and stored in the runtime image label `campaign.cmake.defines` in that same format. The CLI overwrites inherited `CMAKE_DEFINES` environment values.

`recipes` records the SHA256 and size of each recipe file. `recipe_sha256` hashes canonical JSON (sorted keys, compact separators) containing those file identities, all built-in flags, the definitions, and extra targets. Definition values therefore change recipe identity even when recipe bytes are unchanged; reordering definitions does not.

For the GPU budget shim, build with VMM disabled at compile time. From the campaign root, with a clean source checkout at the shown commit and local base images available:

```bash
python3 cc/build_engine/build_engine.py \
  --source ref/llama.cpp --commit 31288c9c66e59377f7788d920678a565bb89dd37 \
  --tag campaign/llamacpp:no-vmm \
  --out artifacts/codexN/no-vmm-build \
  --cmake-define GGML_CUDA_NO_VMM=ON \
  --linkage
```

`--linkage` enables a final check after saving the image and collecting provenance. The saved OCI or classic Docker archive supplies the symbol evidence: layer contents are streamed with blob and rootfs digest checks, whiteouts are merged, and `/app/libggml-cuda.so` (or a versioned variant) is resolved through its link chain. Only the resolved library is copied into a temporary directory, which is removed after inspection. This follows the streaming/whiteout approach in `cc/engine_handoff/engine_handoff.py`, without extracting the image filesystem.

A pure Python ELF reader (`symbols.tool="python-elf"`, `symbols.location="host"`) reads dynamic symbols and `DT_NEEDED`; neither the host nor runtime image needs readelf or nm. It supports ELF32/64 and both byte orders. ELF files without usable dynamic section headers are explicitly unavailable. A pass requires a found library, a `libcudart.so` or `libcudart.so.*` entry in `DT_NEEDED`, and an undefined `cudaMalloc` import. The record also reports undefined `cudaFree`, `cudaMallocAsync`, `cudaFreeAsync`, `cudaMemGetInfo`, and `cuMemCreate` imports; their absence does not fail the check. Defined symbols and lookalike names do not count.

The existing in-image `ldd` probe runs with `docker run --rm --network=none --read-only --entrypoint /bin/sh`, the immutable local `run_ref`, a 60-second client timeout, and no GPU. Its output, return code, and `ldd_libcudart_dynamic` remain separate evidence. Missing runtime tools, failed Docker probes, timeouts, or malformed probe output are recorded without changing the host ELF result. This check does not establish that runtime dependencies resolve on the GPU host.

The record's `linkage` object contains `status` (`not_requested`, `passed`, `failed`, or `unavailable`), `library`, `resolved_library`, config ID, `dt_needed`, `libcudart_dynamic` from `DT_NEEDED`, all six `undefined_imports`, tool return codes/reasons, and output paths. A missing library, invalid archive or ELF, or unreadable dynamic sections is `unavailable`; unavailable measurements are JSON null rather than false.

A failed or unavailable requested check sets top-level `failure_stage="linkage"` and exits 1, while preserving the saved archive and other evidence. `--linkage-optional` enables the same check (even without `--linkage`) but permits a failed/unavailable result with overall success and exit 0; inspect `linkage.status` in that case. With neither flag, linkage is `not_requested`.

The probe saves `linkage.raw.txt` (framed stdout), `linkage.stderr.txt` (Docker/probe stderr), `linkage.ldd.txt`, and `linkage.symbols.txt` (JSON host ELF evidence). The host evidence is saved even if the Docker probe fails; `linkage.ldd.txt` requires a valid probe response. This ELF check does not prove allocation interception, actual pool selection, or GPU execution; the orchestrator must verify `NO_VMM = 1` and allocation events under the budget shim.

## Outputs and failure handling

`build-record.json` uses schema version 2. Version 1 evidence remains untouched; this capability has no build-record reader. Schema 2 adds `cmake_defines`, `recipe_sha256`, and `linkage`; `cmake_flags` includes all built-in and extra definitions. It records status, failure stage/error, requested and resolved commit, Git tree ID and dirty status, patch SHA256 or null, tag/platform, recipe SHA256 and sizes, base references/digests, Docker and Buildx versions, CMake flags, Buildx metadata, image config ID/RepoDigests/Created/Architecture/Os, tool SHA256 values, saved archive SHA256/bytes, build duration and total duration. Fields remain null or empty when a failure occurs before collection. `build_wall_seconds` measures the Bake invocation, including export; `wall_seconds` covers the whole attempt.

The other files are:

- `build.stdout` and `build.stderr`: full subprocess stdout/stderr, including compiler output and diagnostics on failure. Binary Git archive output is directed to staging rather than the logs.
- `buildx-metadata.json`: Buildx metadata, when the build produces it; retained even when the build exits nonzero.
- `engine-image.docker.tar`: `docker save` of the immutable Docker-reported image ID, collected before runtime probes. This ID may identify an OCI index in the containerd store. Its bytes and SHA256 are recorded after saving.

The CLI exits 0 only after all required evidence collection succeeds, otherwise nonzero; `--linkage-optional` permits a recorded linkage failure. Failures include source mismatch/dirty tree, unsupported submodules, malformed or inapplicable patch, unavailable Docker/base image, build/export failure, incorrect architecture, missing binaries, save failure, or malformed archive. A failure after building can leave the tagged local image and partial evidence; inspect `failure_stage` and retry in a fresh output directory. Invalid CLI arguments, an unwritable output path, or a nonempty output directory fail before a record can be created. Existing evidence is never overwritten. The CLI does not push, prune, mount the Docker socket in an image, or operate on unrelated containers. A short-lived `docker run --rm --network=none --read-only --entrypoint /bin/sh` container hashes the tools and libraries without requesting a GPU. After resolving the tag once, saving uses the immutable Docker-reported ID. Before hashing or linkage, the archive inspector follows the OCI catalog and nested indexes to the linux/amd64 image manifest and config, skipping other platforms and attestations. It verifies the SHA256 of referenced JSON blobs and requires exactly one matching config. Classic Docker archives are supported by hashing the config bytes named in `manifest.json`. Hashing and optional linkage then use this config digest as the local `sha256:...` Docker image ID; local-only `repo@digest` references are not used. Buildx `containerimage.config.digest` is optional and is cross-checked against the archive when present. Index metadata is cross-checked when the archive retains the index. Missing, ambiguous, or inconsistent archive identities fail before runtime probes. The record keeps `Id`/`docker_reported_id`, `config_digest`, `manifest_digest`, `index_digest`, `index_manifests`, and `docker_id_in_archive_index` separate; an unavailable manifest or index digest is null. `index.json` is the archive catalog and is not assumed to be the original image index.

Bake requests maximum provenance and saves metadata separately. This does not imply provenance survives image loading and `docker save`. The archive inspector checks `index.json` and reachable OCI manifests for actual in-toto SLSA provenance statements. A classic Docker archive without an OCI index records `retained: false`; an SBOM or an attestation annotation alone does not count. A save or inspection failure leaves provenance unconfirmed. No signature or attestation trust verification is performed.

## Validation without a build

The CLI stages its recipes in `.campaign-recipe/` inside the archived source context. Bake receives digest-pinned base references, source and patch identity, extra targets, and extra definitions from the CLI. Prefer the CLI for validation and evidence collection; direct builds using the older `builds/llamacpp/` recipes do not support these variant options.

From the campaign directory, run:

```bash
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -q \
  cc/build_engine/test_build_engine.py \
  --basetemp=cc/build_engine/.pytest-tmp \
  -o cache_dir=cc/build_engine/.pytest_cache
```

Tests use temporary Git repositories and mocked Docker subprocesses. They cover patch rejection, successful patch isolation, successful record schema, build failure logs/metadata, dirty or mismatched source, archive/tool hashing, provenance versus SBOM, and refusing to overwrite evidence. They also cover define validation, variant recipe identity/build arguments/labels, schema 2, captured ELF linkage fixtures, a tiny host-compiled ELF (crafted fallback without cc), OCI layer whiteouts and symlink chains, host symbol inspection independent of image tools, config-ID versus index-ID targeting, and fatal/optional linkage failures. The T-N2 regression uses the real containerd Buildx metadata fixture without config metadata, plus constructed content-addressed OCI index/manifest/config archives (with another platform and an attestation). It checks config metadata mismatches, missing or corrupt configs, ambiguous configs, and index metadata mismatches before any runtime probe. They use no network, GPU, or real engine build.

This evidence does not prove bitwise reproducibility, runtime correctness, model accuracy, GPU compatibility/performance, or the absence of vulnerabilities. Apt package versions, compiler behavior, timestamps, and upstream build scripts can vary. Base digests and input hashes identify inputs; they do not establish equivalence to an upstream image. The orchestrator must perform the real build and runtime checks. No Docker execution or network access was performed for T-N.
=====
# Placement-aware expert precision (T-PAP)

This recipe quantizes only the experts assigned to CPU at lower precision, while keeping the other experts at Q4_K and ordinary quantizable weights at Q8_0. It is a model-production technique; it needs no inference-engine changes. Norm vectors and expert router matrices remain F32 under upstream quantization policy (`src/llama-quant.cpp:295-314`).

The scratch source is a `git archive` of `ref/llama.cpp` commit `31288c9c66e59377f7788d920678a565bb89dd37`, under `artifacts/codexPAP/tree`. The build is CPU-only, uses `nice -n 10`, and limits compilation and quantization to four threads. No Docker or network is used by the recipe. The evaluation JSON is an orchestrator handoff and does not execute Docker here.

The initial calibration build's automatically generated banner used the parent campaign Git hash `bc22a4f`; its source was still the pinned archive. The recipe explicitly sets `LLAMA_BUILD_COMMIT` and archive build number 0 to prevent this cosmetic provenance error. Initial configure/build logs and the calibration executable hash are retained; the tools are rebuilt with the explicit stamp before model production.

## Integration conditions

Use each `papK_*` with `-ngl 99 --n-cpu-moe K`. In the archived source, `common/arg.cpp:2771-2777` documents the first N layers and calls `llm_add_n_cpu_ffn_overrides`; `common/common.h:1255-1261` actually loops over indices `0 <= i < N`, creating CPU buffer overrides. These citations refer to the pinned scratch source, not an arbitrary later upstream version. GPU-capable evaluation builds must preserve those semantics. Changing K at inference changes which device gets the low-bit weights and invalidates a placement-matched comparison. A CPU-only run cannot measure the intended CPU/GPU division.

The recipe places the specific first-K-layer regex before `ffn_.*_exps=q4_K`. Repeated `--tensor-type REGEX=TYPE` arguments are parsed at `tools/quantize/quantize.cpp:317-347`; `src/llama-quant.cpp:774-785` uses `std::regex_search` and breaks on the first match. Types are case-insensitive. Every output is quantized directly from the read-only BF16 source, with Q8_0 as the base type. No low-bit output is requantized from another low-bit model.

It is not copied into the output directory; the orchestrator must include that basename in the common model directory.

## Reproduction and provenance

Run `cc/pap/make_pap.sh` from any directory. It builds, calibrates, quantizes eight models, verifies actual GGUF tensors using the pinned gguf-py reader, hashes the files, and emits the manifest and lab tests. Individual stages are `build`, `calibrate`, `quantize`, and `verify`. The optional `sanity` stage runs only the CPU pap12_q3 KLD check; run `verify` afterward to include its result in the manifest. Re-running a stage overwrites that stage's outputs. Python requires the already installed NumPy; CMake and the local C/C++ toolchain are used without dependency downloads. Python bytecode writes outside the assignment roots are disabled.

Calibration command (paths expanded in the script):

```sh
nice -n 10 artifacts/codexPAP/build/bin/llama-imatrix \
  -m ~/models/campaign/gguf/granite-3.1-1b-a400m-instruct-bf16.gguf \
  -f ~/models/campaign/data/wikitext/wikitext-2-raw/wiki.train.raw \
  -o artifacts/codexPAP/models/granite-wtrain.imatrix \
  --output-format gguf -t 6 -tb 6 -ngl 0 -c 512 --chunks 100 --no-ppl \
  --output-frequency 10
```

The imatrix uses only the first 100 processed TRAIN chunks; TEST is not used for calibration. It is GGUF format despite the requested `.imatrix` suffix. `MANIFEST.json` records the imatrix metadata, completed chunks, TRAIN and TEST SHA256 hashes, source and output hashes, sizes, and each tensor's actual type and dimensions. `logs/imatrix.log` records the run; calibration start/end files record UTC timestamps. The train/test distinction is dataset provenance, not a claim of zero overlapping natural-language strings.

## Evaluation handoff

`artifacts/codexPAP/lab-tests-pap.json` contains 22 tests using exactly the existing lab entry shapes. All `model_file` references are basenames.

The orchestrator must register this JSON in the lab's test-definition directory, place the eight outputs and existing mixE4K baseline in one model directory, and supply `--data ~/models/campaign/data/wikitext/wikitext-2-raw/wiki.test.raw` when submitting KLD tests. Registration and lab execution are outside this assignment's write locations. Existing absolute read-only prompt/KL mounts match the supplied lab templates.

- Six placement-matched decode runs for calibrated PAP outputs; one for `pap24_q3_noimat` at K=24; three for `mix4_imat`; three for mixE4K. Decode copies `lab/tests/match1.json`: `llama-completion -f /tin/chat.txt -n 160 -c 4096 --temp 0 -s 1 -ngl 99 -no-cnv --no-warmup --n-cpu-moe K`, with the read-only `artifacts/traces/in:/tin:ro` mount.
- Nine KLD runs, covering every produced model and mixE4K. Each copies `lab/tests/mem2.json`'s `kl_q8`: `llama-perplexity -c 512 --chunks 20 -ngl 99 --kl-divergence-base /out/bf16.kl --kl-divergence`, with `needs_data: true`, parser `kl`, and read-only `artifacts/kl:/out:ro` mount. The lab supplies WikiText-2 TEST through its standard data handling. Saved KL data also carries its evaluation tokens.

The full GPU lab suite is defined here for orchestrator execution. Any optional CPU sanity outcome is recorded separately in `artifacts/codexPAP/cpu-sanity.json` and in the manifest; it is not a substitute for the suite. The BF16 KL header is checked against the pinned reader's format (`tools/perplexity/perplexity.cpp:1688-1714`).

## Claims allowed

Verified type placement, byte reductions, calibration provenance, and content hashes are factory properties. The hypothesis is that smaller CPU expert weights reduce DRAM traffic during decode; speedup need not scale with file size because kernels, routing, caching, and GPU work also contribute. File size does not establish resident host RAM or VRAM. Calibration is intended to reduce low-bit quality loss; that benefit must be measured against the controls. Do not claim throughput improvement, memory residency savings, acceptable quality for all variants, or an imatrix quality improvement without completed corresponding lab results. A WikiText CPU sanity KLD, if present, supports only that model and dataset, not task-level quality.

def emit(agent, rec):
    path = os.path.join(ROOT, "evidence", f"{agent}.jsonl")
    line = (json.dumps(rec, sort_keys=True) + "\n").encode()
    fd = os.open(path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_APPEND | os.O_CREAT, 0o644)

        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX); os.write(fd, line); os.fsync(fd)

def survivors(sid):
    """processes still alive in the command's session (descendants that outlived the main process)"""
    out = []

# Model inspection

`inspect_model.py` uses Python 3.12, numpy, and the pinned local
`ref/llama.cpp/gguf-py`. It reads that reference tree without writing caches.
It never reads, dequantizes, copies, or hashes tensor payloads. A read-only
file mapping provides metadata parsing; its tensor-construction hook is
replaced with shape/type accounting, and the mapping closes after inspection.
No builds, GPU work, worker pools, or model inference are required.

From the campaign root:

```bash
OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
  python cc/model_inspect/inspect_model.py \
  ~/models/campaign/gguf/granite-3.1-1b-a400m-instruct-mixE4K.gguf \
  --trace experiments/routing/prose.json \
  --out artifacts/codexMI/granite-mixE4K.json --summary
```

The Python API is `inspect(gguf_path, trace=None) -> dict`, with
`schema: "model-stats/0"`. Without `--out` or `--summary`, the CLI writes JSON
to stdout. `--summary` prints a human-readable Markdown table; use `--out`
alongside it to retain the full machine report. Missing paths or invalid
headers/traces produce a nonzero exit. Output parent directories must exist.

## Accounting conventions

- Shapes use GGML order (`ne[0]` is the contiguous dimension), the reverse of
  numpy shape order. Bytes are exact tensor payload bytes from integer shape
  products and `GGML_QUANT_SIZES`; file headers and alignment gaps are excluded.

Classification key: MP = Manager policy | LP = lab-provider behaviour | CC = reusable CC operation | CMP = component | AM = agent methodology. Anything not listed as demonstrated is "not demonstrated".
1. **Raw bytes in, decode only at the parser; parser errors never kill the runner** (MP+LP). Event: job-8df3c7bb27 att-1 died with UnicodeDecodeError in assess(); reconcile marked it interrupted, nothing scored (D020). T-M: assess() reads bytes, flags `invalid_utf8=true`, converts any parser exception into `assessment_error` while exit code/elapsed/mem are still recorded; stdout/stderr files are never rewritten. Orchestrator policy: invalid UTF-8 in GENERATED text is flagged, not failed (att-2 st_prose_n18 flagged invalid_utf8 and still scored, D022); a flagged output is never silently clean. Demonstrated on att-2 (10/10) and 17 CPU-only tests; Docker/GPU runner path under T-M was mock-tested only by Codex.
2. **Per-test input identity** (LP). Event: job-8df3c7bb27 hashed the bf16 GGUF while every test loaded mixE4K, so the model actually used was unverified (D021 gap). T-Q: submit records `spec.inputs` (every model_file hash, referenced prompt/data file hashes from ro mounts, per-test definition hash); re-verified in the preparing phase, mismatch -> not_started; legacy specs keep their idempotency check and run with `inputs_unverified=true`. Limits: literal argument paths only, no indirect dependencies, no check after verification. 48 CPU-only tests; not run against a live job.
3. **A rerun is a new attempt, never a relabel** (MP). Event: D020 was completed as job-8df3c7bb27 att-2; att-1 stays `interrupted` with its partial output. Same rule as earlier retry-as-new (job-9252e2d8bf att-2).
4. **Memory-budget guarantee taxonomy** (MP). Classes: none | cooperative-intercept | cgroup-host | hard. The gpu_budget LD_PRELOAD shim is cooperative-intercept only: bypassable via VMM pool (cuMemCreate), static cudart, cuGetProcAddress, other processes (D021). With NO_VMM it counted weights 778.7 + KV 192 + compute 108 MiB (peak 1078.9) vs ~1388 MiB nvidia-smi delta, ~310 MiB uncounted (D023). # Q8 activation reuse campaign patch

Apply only to llama.cpp `31288c9c66e59377f7788d920678a565bb89dd37`. See [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) for the safety rule and exclusions. This directory contains the patch and its handoff documentation; no reference-source files were edited.

## Build CC

From the campaign root, the orchestrator can build with the existing Build CC:

```bash
python3 cc/build_engine/build_engine.py \
  --source ref/llama.cpp --commit 31288c9c6 \
  --patch cc/q8_reuse/q8-activation-reuse.patch \
  --tag campaign/llamacpp:c1-q8-reuse \
  --out artifacts/codexH/build-q8-reuse
```

Use a fresh/empty output directory and the Build CC's required locally available, digest-pinned CUDA bases. Build a separate unpatched image from the same commit/toolchain for baseline comparison. The Build CC archives the source and applies the patch to its staging copy. Docker and CUDA were not run for this assignment.

## A/B switch

Reuse defaults ON. The environment setting is read once per process. Start separate processes for each run:

```bash
GGML_CUDA_Q8_REUSE=0 /app/llama-bench -m "$MODEL_Q8" -ngl 99 -p 0 -n 128 -b 1 -ub 1
GGML_CUDA_Q8_REUSE=1 /app/llama-bench -m "$MODEL_Q8" -ngl 99 -p 0 -n 128 -b 1 -ub 1
```

These commands assume the patched tools and model are available at the indicated runtime paths. When launching through Docker, forward the switch with `-e GGML_CUDA_Q8_REUSE=0` or `=1`. An unset switch enables reuse; other values, including `false`, also enable it. Keep model, workload, clocks, threads and all flags identical across runs. Record warmup and repeated decode measurements; do not infer a gain from the patch alone.

## Required validation before acceptance

1. Compile the patch with nvcc in the target Build CC. Run `test-backend-ops` for CUDA/CPU matmul correctness, including one-token Q8_0 and control types/batches. No CUDA compile result is available yet.
2. Compare the unpatched Q8_0 baseline, patched OFF and patched ON with identical model/corpus/options. The assignment requires mean KLD **0** and **100% same top-1** using `llama-perplexity --kl-divergence-base`. Force `-b 1 -ub 1` so the check exercises the changed decode path, rather than only prompt MMQ. For example, with host paths to the built binaries:

   ```bash
   "$BASELINE_BIN/llama-perplexity" -m "$MODEL_Q8" -f "$CORPUS" \
     -ngl 99 -c 128 -b 1 -ub 1 --chunks 4 \
     --kl-divergence-base artifacts/codexH/baseline.kld

   GGML_CUDA_Q8_REUSE=0 "$PATCHED_BIN/llama-perplexity" \
     -m "$MODEL_Q8" -f "$CORPUS" -ngl 99 -c 128 -b 1 -ub 1 --chunks 4 \
     --kl-divergence-base artifacts/codexH/baseline.kld --kl-divergence

   GGML_CUDA_Q8_REUSE=1 "$PATCHED_BIN/llama-perplexity" \
     -m "$MODEL_Q8" -f "$CORPUS" -ngl 99 -c 128 -b 1 -ub 1 --chunks 4 \
     --kl-divergence-base artifacts/codexH/baseline.kld --kl-divergence
   ```

   **Tool limitation:** this revision saves clipped, uint16-quantized log probabilities, not lossless raw logits (`tools/perplexity/perplexity.cpp`, the two `log_softmax` overloads). A baseline-versus-itself KLD run may therefore report a small nonzero mean and quantization can obscure top-1 ties. Run that self-comparison too. Do not declare bit identity from a rounded KLD number or silently waive the requested zero gate. Report discrepancies and the self-comparison floor to the orchestrator.

3. Independently compare every raw F32 logit byte against baseline and patched OFF using a lossless logits-dumping harness (`llama_get_logits_ith` for each evaluated token). Require byte-for-byte equality, not a tolerance. Include repeated one-token evaluations with changing inputs/positions, enough calls for graph warmup/capture/replay, and graph/shape switches that grow scratch sizes then return to an older captured graph. Repeat with `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1` and with its variable **unset** to enable graphs; this backend treats any set value, including `0`, as disabling graphs.
4. Exercise allocator alias hazards in backend graphs: repeated use of one input, distinct tensor identities sharing an address, partial-overlap output views, an intervening writer reusing input storage, and successive evaluations that reuse the same tensor object/address with new values. Verify that overlapping RoPE, successful fusion, other operations, and concurrent-stream graphs cannot reuse a stale entry. Check MoE and fused paths as unchanged controls.
5. Profile kernel launches and decode throughput for ON versus OFF. In an unfused Q/RoPE/K/V safe window with the same input, expect one quantization instead of three. Fused operations and other writers end the window, so model-level savings must be measured. Check no regression in disabled, non-Q8_0 and multi-token paths. Capture/replay and pointer-lifetime checks are mandatory even if direct execution passes.

## Checks performed here

- Confirmed reference HEAD is the target commit and its tracked working tree is clean.
- `git apply --check --verbose` passed on a `git archive` copy under `artifacts/codexH/verification-tree`, with Git discovery stopped before the enclosing campaign repository. All three intended files were checked.
- Applied the patch to that copy and compared all three resulting files against the edited work copies; reverse application check passed.
- Host smoke checks passed with C++17, `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`, AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, for unset, `0`, `1` and `false` switch settings. LeakSanitizer was disabled because it cannot run under the sandbox's ptrace. These mocks do not validate CUDA compilation or GPU arithmetic.

Evidence and repeatable host checks: `artifacts/codexH/validation.txt`, `host_check.py`, `host_check.cpp`, and `make_patch.py`. Runtime numerical/performance gates remain pending with the orchestrator.

network access, or privileged container options. It is an experiment control,
not a security boundary or a limit on physical VRAM reported by `nvidia-smi`.

The assignment's approximate scale is `128/500 * 2.67 GiB ≈ 700 MiB`.

## Configuration and accounting

| Variable | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `GPU_BUDGET_MIB` | Unsigned integer binary MiB. Absent: no cap and real memory-info values. `0`: no positive-size allocations. |
| `GPU_BUDGET_RESERVE_MIB` | Default 0. Effective allocation capacity is `max(budget - reserve, 0)`. |
| `GPU_BUDGET_COUNT_MANAGED` | `1` (default): charge requested managed bytes immediately, without tracking residency/prefetch. `0`: managed memory is outside the budget. |
| `GPU_BUDGET_LOG` | Optional writable JSONL path, opened in append mode. All events are flushed immediately, including denials, plus a final summary at normal exit/unload. |

Configuration is read once on first intercepted outer call. Malformed integers,
overflow, invalid managed settings, or an unopenable requested log terminate
with exit 125 rather than silently dropping the restriction. Each process has
its own cap and must have its own log path for unambiguous records.

`cudaMemGetInfo` and `cuMemGetInfo_v2` first invoke the real API so normal
initialization and invalid-argument/context errors are preserved. After success,
`total = budget`, `free = max(budget - reserve, 0) - used`. Allocation accounting
uses successful requested bytes, with padding included for pitched storage.
No allocation is issued when that amount exceeds the remaining capacity.
Underlying CUDA allocation failures leave the counter unchanged. Denials return
`cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` or `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY`; output arguments on
failure must not be used. A missing real entry point returns NOT_SUPPORTED.
Synthetic failures return the specified error directly; they do not update
cudart's private last-error state for `cudaGetLastError`/`cudaPeekAtLastError`.

A mutex serializes decisions, real calls, and pointer-hash-table updates. A
thread-local nesting guard prevents runtime→driver calls from charging twice.
Bookkeeping storage is reserved before invoking an allocator; metadata OOM is
also an allocation denial. Successful frees of unknown pointers are passed
through and do not change the balance. Failed frees retain their charge.

`cudaFreeAsync` and `cuMemFreeAsync` **synchronize their stream after enqueueing
the free** before returning budget to the counter. They therefore block and
alter async performance/ordering. Stream synchronization errors retain the
charge conservatively, even if the underlying free eventually completes; the
balance may stay lower until process exit. No event polling or background
reaper is used. Async allocation is charged immediately on successful enqueue.

`cudaMallocPitch` and `cudaMalloc3D`, while the cap is enabled, synthesize linear
storage through real `cudaMalloc`. Pitch is rounded to at least 512 bytes and
the device's texture and texture-pitch alignments, and checked against maximum
pitch. The charged size is `pitch * height [* depth]`, checked for overflow.
Returned `xsize`/`ysize` retain requested extents. This avoids speculative
over-budget allocations, but pitch can differ from native cudart. Pitched
allocation with zero extents is rejected. Texture-specific uses and exact
native pitch compatibility require validation on the target GPU; the intended
llama.cpp path uses ordinary `cudaMalloc`.

The JSONL fields are `event`, `api`, `pointer` (hex string), `bytes`, `used`,
`peak`, `budget`, `reserve`, `capacity`, and numeric `status`. Events are
`init`, `alloc`, `free`, `deny`, `error`, and `exit`. `used`/`peak` exclude the
reserve. Opted-out managed allocations still log their requested size without
changing counters; their frees are unknown-size (`bytes=0`) events.
No summary is guaranteed for SIGKILL, `_exit`, or fatal crashes;
already-flushed events survive. Atexit and destructor share an idempotent
finalizer, so ordinary exit logs the summary once.

## Coverage and limitations

Covered exported symbols:

| API family | Symbols |
| --- | --- |
| Runtime allocation | `cudaMalloc`, `cudaMallocAsync`, `cudaMallocPitch`, `cudaMalloc3D`, `cudaMallocManaged` |
| Runtime free/info | `cudaFree`, `cudaFreeAsync`, `cudaMemGetInfo` |
| Driver allocation | `cuMemAlloc_v2`, `cuMemAllocAsync` |
| Driver free/info | `cuMemFree_v2`, `cuMemFreeAsync`, `cuMemGetInfo_v2` |

**Not covered:** `cuMemCreate` / `cuMemRelease` and VMM mappings; arrays and
mipmapped arrays; `cuMemAllocManaged`, driver pitched allocation, explicit
`*FromPoolAsync`; IPC/imported/external allocations; host allocation/mapping
(`cudaHostAlloc`, `cudaHostRegister`, mapped host memory); per-thread-default-
stream `_ptsz` symbols and legacy unversioned driver ABI symbols; direct
`cuGetProcAddress`/`cudaGetDriverEntryPoint` lookups; deep-bound or statically
linked CUDA; and allocation/context cleanup through `cudaDeviceReset` or
context destruction. Do not reset/destroy contexts while tracked allocations
remain live. Start a new process between trials. Forking after CUDA/shim
initialization and CUDA graph capture/replay are unsupported.

VMM is deliberately left unsupported: releasing a generic allocation handle
does **not** release physical storage while mappings survive. This checkout's
llama.cpp maps each allocation then immediately calls `cuMemRelease`, so a
simple handle-only wrapper would falsely restore the budget. Correct coverage
would also require mapping lifetimes, aliases, imports, retained handles, and
partial unmaps. Until that exists, build with VMM disabled as described above.

CUDA context/cuBLAS workspace overhead (approximately 300 MiB, device and
version dependent), internal driver/cudart allocations, kernels' local memory,
allocation granularity, and pool caches/reserved memory are **not counted**.
Pools may retain physical memory after a charged logical allocation is freed.
To leave room for estimated overhead within a 700 MiB experiment envelope, use
`GPU_BUDGET_MIB=700 GPU_BUDGET_RESERVE_MIB=300`: total reports 700 MiB and initial
free is 400 MiB. If 700 MiB should be available specifically to intercepted
allocations, leave reserve at 0 and allow overhead outside that amount.
Measure the real overhead separately; the reserve is an estimate, not telemetry.

# Placement-aware expert precision (T-PAP)

This recipe quantizes only the experts assigned to CPU at lower precision, while keeping the other experts at Q4_K and ordinary quantizable weights at Q8_0. It is a model-production technique; it needs no inference-engine changes. Norm vectors and expert router matrices remain F32 under upstream quantization policy (`src/llama-quant.cpp:295-314`).

The scratch source is a `git archive` of `ref/llama.cpp` commit `31288c9c66e59377f7788d920678a565bb89dd37`, under `artifacts/codexPAP/tree`. The build is CPU-only, uses `nice -n 10`, and limits compilation and quantization to four threads. No Docker or network is used by the recipe. The evaluation JSON is an orchestrator handoff and does not execute Docker here.

The initial calibration build's automatically generated banner used the parent campaign Git hash `bc22a4f`; its source was still the pinned archive. The recipe explicitly sets `LLAMA_BUILD_COMMIT` and archive build number 0 to prevent this cosmetic provenance error. Initial configure/build logs and the calibration executable hash are retained; the tools are rebuilt with the explicit stamp before model production.

Use each `papK_*` with `-ngl 99 --n-cpu-moe K`. In the archived source, `common/arg.cpp:2771-2777` documents the first N layers and calls `llm_add_n_cpu_ffn_overrides`; `common/common.h:1255-1261` actually loops over indices `0 <= i < N`, creating CPU buffer overrides. These citations refer to the pinned scratch source, not an arbitrary later upstream version. GPU-capable evaluation builds must preserve those semantics. Changing K at inference changes which device gets the low-bit weights and invalidates a placement-matched comparison. A CPU-only run cannot measure the intended CPU/GPU division.

The recipe places the specific first-K-layer regex before `ffn_.*_exps=q4_K`. Types are case-insensitive. Every output is quantized directly from the read-only BF16 source, with Q8_0 as the base type. No low-bit output is requantized from another low-bit model.

# Frozen-protocol experiment (campaign/lab)

Principle: write the acceptance rule down and commit it BEFORE any timed result exists; then the numbers decide. Run from `campaign/`.
Scripts in `.claude/skills/frozen-experiment/scripts/`: `make_order.py`, `agg.py`, `loadmon.sh`. One GPU job at a time; no compiles,
downloads or CPU inference during a timing window (a download alone gave 10-15% spreads in D035; compiles distort CPU-expert speeds, D015).

## 1. Protocol note (decisions/D0xx, written first)
Model on D026/D027/D032. State: candidate + patch sha256; image(s) and run_ref; models (+sha); the PRIMARY comparison (same binary, switch OFF vs ON
removes build variance, D026); tests file + order file; control arms (e.g. `staticflags` = same flags without the candidate, D027); acceptance
numbers (e.g. decode >= +2% / +5% beyond the observed ~3% spread, GPU MiB within +3%, KLD <= threshold, text/PPL identity); what
"rejected/inconclusive" means; the claim category it will get (see `decision-note`). Amendments are dated and made BEFORE timed results (D027 amendment 1).
Commit the note + tests + order file. (D026 was frozen in commit 474be3b.)

## 2. Tests JSON (`lab/tests/<exp>.json`)
One new file per experiment; copy entries from `match1.json` (decode: `llama-completion -f /tin/chat.txt -n 160 -c 4096 --temp 0 -s 1 -ngl 99 -no-cnv --no-warmup`
with `docker_args` `-v <campaign>/artifacts/traces/in:/tin:ro`), `c1q8.json` (`llama-bench -p 0 -n 128 -r 10 -o json`, parser `bench_json`, `env` switch), `pap1.json`/`mem2.json`
(KLD: `llama-perplexity -c 512 --chunks 20 --kl-divergence-base /out/bf16.kl --kl-divergence`, `needs_data: true`, mount `artifacts/kl:/out:ro`), `kv1.json` (PPL).
- Test names are global: `load_tests()` merges ALL `lab/tests/*.json` with `dict.update` - a duplicate name silently overwrites. Prefix names (`pap_`, `c1_`).
- `model_file` per test (basename in the model dir) lets one job compare models; `env` carries engine switches; absolute paths for ro mounts.
- Same prompt/seed/-c for every arm; declare cold/warm cache (`cold_cache`) if memory is measured.

## 3. Alternating order
```bash
S=.claude/skills/frozen-experiment/scripts
python3 $S/make_order.py --group a_n24,a_n18,a_n12 --rounds 3 --once kl_a,kl_b --out artifacts/x2/<exp>-order.txt
```
Per group, round i forward if even else reversed (pair, 2 rounds = ABBA); `--repeat N` repeats all groups (c1: `--group q8_tg_r0,q8_tg_r1 --group ... --rounds 2 --repeat 2`);
`--once` = deterministic quality tests run once. Verified to regenerate `pap1`, `c1`, `match1`, `hsplit1` order files byte-for-byte. 3 rounds minimum; keep the
same job for all arms.

## 4. Submit, monitor, run
```bash
export CAMPAIGN_ID=c1
# monitor FIRST; validate it (below), then:
nohup $S/loadmon.sh artifacts/x2/<exp>-hostload.log >/dev/null 2>&1 & MON=$!
JOB=$(bin/lab submit --image llamacpp-b0 --model $PWD/<model>.gguf [--data ~/models/campaign/data/wikitext/wikitext-2-raw/wiki.test.raw] \
      --tests $(cat artifacts/x2/<exp>-order.txt) --key <EXP>-alt-1 --res timeout_s=600)
bin/run_op --agent claude-code --task X4 --desc "<exp> timed job $JOB" -- bin/lab run $JOB > artifacts/x2/<exp>-run.out 2>&1
kill $MON; $S/loadmon.sh --summary artifacts/x2/<exp>-hostload.log
```
- `--data` is REQUIRED when any test has `needs_data` (submit fails otherwise). `--key` makes submit idempotent; job.json embeds the test definitions
  and per-input hashes (D025/T-Q), so edits to `lab/tests/` after submit do not change the job. A rerun is a new attempt (`att-2`), never a relabel.
- Image names: `bin/lab image add NAME <build-record image.run_ref>` (see `engine-candidate`); `llamacpp-b0` is the baseline.
- Chains of several jobs: copy `artifacts/x2/chain3.sh` (wait for a build record, submit/run sequentially, one monitor around all).
- Monitor validation: baseline must read `cc=0`; positive control from a SEPARATE command: `cp /bin/sleep /tmp/cc1plus; /tmp/cc1plus 8 &` must raise `cc` to 1.
  The `[c]c1plus` bracket pattern stops pgrep matching the monitor itself (the first monitor reported a phantom compiler). Note a
  command line that merely contains the word `cc1plus` (your own shell wrapper) also matches. A window with compilers/downloads active is labelled UNTIMED / PROVISIONAL.

## 5. Aggregate
```bash
python3 $S/agg.py $JOB                                  # per-test n, gpu MiB, host MiB, medians dec/pre/ppl/kld/top1/tg/pp, [min-max]
python3 $S/agg.py $JOB --strip _r0,_r1 --compare c1_q8_tg_r0=c1_q8_tg_r1   # % delta of medians
python3 $S/agg.py $JOB --json > artifacts/x2/<exp>-agg.json
.claude/skills/engine-candidate/scripts/text_fp.py $JOB --filter gen         # text identity per test
```
Refuse to score unless the header shows `N/N` clean (`tests_completed_cleanly == tests_expected`). Check `BAD` counts, the spread vs the effect size,
disjoint ranges for small effects, and the host-load summary. Tested on job-ad883810b3 (D022), job-34c09bec98 (D029: tg +2.07%), job-3d2fbbd061 (D035).

## 6. Verdict
Apply the frozen rule literally; report accepted / rejected / inconclusive with numbers and ranges, the unmet criterion, and any provisional flag.
Write `decisions/D0xx-...md` with `decision-note`. Register nothing as a claim outside the frozen scope.

import argparse, json, os, re, subprocess, sys
