What correlates and what doesn't

Strong, usable relationships

  • 1/decode is linear in bytes moved off the GPU. On Qwen each CPU layer adds 0.757 ms, which is about 30 GB/s, and the line holds from K=8 to K=48 (D039).
  • VRAM is linear in K: about 347 MiB per Qwen layer and 27 MiB per Granite layer. Planner MiB error is under 0.3%.
  • Cache hit rate decides cache vs static. Upload-mode cache wins when held-out coverage is about 70% or higher. CPU-share removes most of the miss penalty, so it wins much lower.
  • Expert size × handoff cost decides granularity. Crossover = fixed cost / per-byte cost (D031).
  • Paired KLD tracks quality where unpaired PPL can't (stderr 0.0015 vs 0.37).
  • imatrix → lower KLD at every bit width (−33% at 4-bit, −13% at 3-bit).
  • Copy-heavy text → speculation acceptance. Rewrite and repeat prompts give 2.4–3×; chat gives none.
  • Routing locality ranks code > prose > chat on both Granite and Qwen traces.

Weak, misleading or absent

  • Fewer bits ≠ faster on CPU. Q3_K unpacking is compute-bound on AVX2, so 3-bit was only +1.5%.
  • Greedy text identity ≠ quality. Every placement changes the text. The same config can even change it between runs (62290c73 vs 77a3045a).
  • Harness speedups ≠ integrated speedups. The integrated graph pays per-layer fixed costs (D030).
  • Proxy-model results ≠ target results. Granite results flipped on Qwen twice (D022, the planner).
  • Kernel count ≠ bandwidth. 40–46% of kernel time is in tiny kernels at under 1% DRAM.
  • Cache-policy choice barely matters. LRU, SLRU and ClassLRU are within 2 points. Budget and miss handling matter far more.
  • Profiled time ≠ real time. Node tracing inflates gaps 3×, and ncu serialises kernels.
  • Identical bytes in a different file vary ±5%, so effects under 5% need A/A and alternation.
  • A reported hit rate can mislead (Strata: PCIe-served experts are not counted).

Structure vs flexibility

The campaign settled into two speeds. Unfrozen screens find things quickly, and frozen protocols decide whether to accept them. Each side caught errors the other would have missed.

Where structure paid off

  • The frozen quiet-host rerun retracted PAP (+9.8% → +1.5%) before it reached the factory.
  • The plan → measure loop caught the planner's 5% decode optimism on its first run.
  • Engagement checks caught static-hot never running. Without them it would have been timed as "no gain".
  • run_ref image identity fixed the wrong-image-id bug (D016).
  • Plausibility guards rejected 1384 GB/s before it fed the planner.
  • The A/A interference check let downloads run during timing at a measured 0.2% cost.
  • Recorded ops made every number here traceable to a command.

Where flexibility paid off

  • An hour-long unfrozen screen found the +38% cache win that overturned D022.
  • Research intake found ngram-mod (2.4–3× for free) and upstream cpu-share, which flipped 4 GB tonight.
  • Rebasing to upstream (519 commits) brought levers we would have spent days building.
  • bpftrace and perf were set up ad hoc in minutes and confirmed the CPU-layer cost by a second method.
  • Delegating to Codex let six tools run in parallel (POL, SPECM, PROFW, CAL2, VER, PL4).

Where structure cost too much

  • Hand-written test JSON per experiment led to a scripted runner instead of bin/lab.
  • A text-identity criterion in E2/E4 may reject lossless speculation (G11).
  • Mocked fixtures passed tests and failed on real output 3 times.
  • A wait-gate meant to keep the host quiet deadlocked the overnight chain.

Rule of thumb: be strict about identity, provenance, engagement, noise floors and acceptance criteria. Be flexible about where ideas come from, which engine is the base, and how a screen is run. Of the 43 notes, about 6 are infra bugs, 4 are user directives, 6 are frozen protocols and about 27 are results. Every result that later reversed came from a proxy model, a harness or a noisy window.

Expected vs unexpected

Went as expected

  • Decode is memory-bandwidth-bound wherever experts live.
  • Quantization quality ordering: Q8 ≈ lossless, 4-bit costs a little, 2-bit collapses.
  • CUDA graphs help (4.2%). Small-kernel fusion has headroom.
  • KV q8_0 halves KV cost at no quality cost once fixed.
  • Speculation gains depend on the workload.

Surprised us

  • The expert cache flipped from loser (Granite) to winner (Qwen), then won at 4 GB too once misses could stay on the CPU.
  • Per-layer handoff, not bytes, dominated Granite decode (GPU idle 80%).
  • 3-bit experts were barely faster on the CPU.
  • Qwen3 thinking mode silently disabled n-gram drafting.
  • The handoff estimate varies 4× depending on the method (52–199 µs).
  • Zen 2 exposes no DRAM counters to perf on this kernel.
  • The same config gave different greedy text between runs.
  • Provider refusals were triggered by crash/debug wording in a Codex brief.

Rough base rates

  • Of 23 written predictions: 8 confirmed, 4 magnitude off, 4 reversed, 7 silent failures.
  • Anything that transfers from proxy to target: about half reversed or were off by more than 2×.
  • First-run tooling on real output: about 1 in 2 needed a fix (CAL1, CAL2, T-CAL CPU probe, ngram, chain).
  • Same-model, in-range predictions: almost always within 10%.

Methodologies

Measurement

  • Pre-register, then measure. Freeze the protocol before results exist.
  • A/A first to get the noise floor, then matched A/B in ABBA order with medians.
  • Quiet host: no compiles, Codex runs or unthrottled downloads. Check it per arm and label the arm otherwise.
  • Rerun anything provisional that came from a noisy window.
  • Profile with a perturbation check against unprofiled timing.
  • Sample peak VRAM from outside the process (nvidia-smi every 0.5 s).

Correctness

  • Engagement before timing: prove the code path ran with counters or log lines.
  • Text identity for exact rewrites. KLD/PPL for anything numerical, including placement.
  • Paired KLD vs reference logits. Never unpaired PPL alone.
  • test-backend-ops for every patched op.
  • Sort every claim into a category: full-engine gain, representation trade-off, placement-only, or failed.

Modeling and transfer

  • Label each result transferable or proxy-only. Proxy results are hypotheses on the target.
  • Predict from bytes and measured constants, and say "extrapolated" outside the calibration range.
  • Report fixed per-layer cost next to per-byte cost.
  • Plausibility guards on every microbenchmark (no faster-than-peak numbers).
  • Leave one model out before trusting a fit.

Process and delegation

  • Opus orchestrates. Codex does bounded work from written assignments and is reviewed against real records.
  • Capture real tool output as fixtures. Mocks hide real failures.
  • Every action goes through run_op, so every number has a command.
  • Research intake → smallest probe → indicative screen → frozen experiment → planner lever.
  • Avoid pgrep/pkill patterns that can match their own command line.

What correlates and what doesn't

Strong, usable relationships

  • 1/decode is linear in bytes moved off the GPU. On Qwen each CPU layer adds 0.757 ms, which is about 30 GB/s, and the line holds from K=8 to K=48 (D039).
  • VRAM is linear in K: about 347 MiB per Qwen layer and 27 MiB per Granite layer. Planner MiB error is under 0.3%.
  • Cache hit rate decides cache vs static. Upload-mode cache wins when held-out coverage is about 70% or higher. CPU-share removes most of the miss penalty, so it wins much lower.
  • Expert size × handoff cost decides granularity. Crossover = fixed cost / per-byte cost (D031).
  • Paired KLD tracks quality where unpaired PPL can't (stderr 0.0015 vs 0.37).
  • imatrix → lower KLD at every bit width (−33% at 4-bit, −13% at 3-bit).
  • Copy-heavy text → speculation acceptance. Rewrite and repeat prompts give 2.4–3×; chat gives none.
  • Routing locality ranks code > prose > chat on both Granite and Qwen traces.

Weak, misleading or absent

  • Fewer bits ≠ faster on CPU. Q3_K unpacking is compute-bound on AVX2, so 3-bit was only +1.5%.
  • Greedy text identity ≠ quality. Every placement changes the text. The same config can even change it between runs (62290c73 vs 77a3045a).
  • Harness speedups ≠ integrated speedups. The integrated graph pays per-layer fixed costs (D030).
  • Proxy-model results ≠ target results. Granite results flipped on Qwen twice (D022, the planner).
  • Kernel count ≠ bandwidth. 40–46% of kernel time is in tiny kernels at under 1% DRAM.
  • Cache-policy choice barely matters. LRU, SLRU and ClassLRU are within 2 points. Budget and miss handling matter far more.
  • Profiled time ≠ real time. Node tracing inflates gaps 3×, and ncu serialises kernels.
  • Identical bytes in a different file vary ±5%, so effects under 5% need A/A and alternation.
  • A reported hit rate can mislead (Strata: PCIe-served experts are not counted).

Structure vs flexibility

The campaign settled into two speeds. Unfrozen screens find things quickly, and frozen protocols decide whether to accept them. Each side caught errors the other would have missed.

Where structure paid off

  • The frozen quiet-host rerun retracted PAP (+9.8% → +1.5%) before it reached the factory.
  • The plan → measure loop caught the planner's 5% decode optimism on its first run.
  • Engagement checks caught static-hot never running. Without them it would have been timed as "no gain".
  • run_ref image identity fixed the wrong-image-id bug (D016).
  • Plausibility guards rejected 1384 GB/s before it fed the planner.
  • The A/A interference check let downloads run during timing at a measured 0.2% cost.
  • Recorded ops made every number here traceable to a command.

Where flexibility paid off

  • An hour-long unfrozen screen found the +38% cache win that overturned D022.
  • Research intake found ngram-mod (2.4–3× for free) and upstream cpu-share, which flipped 4 GB tonight.
  • Rebasing to upstream (519 commits) brought levers we would have spent days building.
  • bpftrace and perf were set up ad hoc in minutes and confirmed the CPU-layer cost by a second method.
  • Delegating to Codex let six tools run in parallel (POL, SPECM, PROFW, CAL2, VER, PL4).

Where structure cost too much

  • Hand-written test JSON per experiment led to a scripted runner instead of bin/lab.
  • A text-identity criterion in E2/E4 may reject lossless speculation (G11).
  • Mocked fixtures passed tests and failed on real output 3 times.
  • A wait-gate meant to keep the host quiet deadlocked the overnight chain.

Rule of thumb: be strict about identity, provenance, engagement, noise floors and acceptance criteria. Be flexible about where ideas come from, which engine is the base, and how a screen is run. Of the 43 notes, about 6 are infra bugs, 4 are user directives, 6 are frozen protocols and about 27 are results. Every result that later reversed came from a proxy model, a harness or a noisy window.

Expected vs unexpected

Went as expected

  • Decode is memory-bandwidth-bound wherever experts live.
  • Quantization quality ordering: Q8 ≈ lossless, 4-bit costs a little, 2-bit collapses.
  • CUDA graphs help (4.2%). Small-kernel fusion has headroom.
  • KV q8_0 halves KV cost at no quality cost once fixed.
  • Speculation gains depend on the workload.

Surprised us

  • The expert cache flipped from loser (Granite) to winner (Qwen), then won at 4 GB too once misses could stay on the CPU.
  • Per-layer handoff, not bytes, dominated Granite decode (GPU idle 80%).
  • 3-bit experts were barely faster on the CPU.
  • Qwen3 thinking mode silently disabled n-gram drafting.
  • The handoff estimate varies 4× depending on the method (52–199 µs).
  • Zen 2 exposes no DRAM counters to perf on this kernel.
  • The same config gave different greedy text between runs.
  • Provider refusals were triggered by crash/debug wording in a Codex brief.

Rough base rates

  • Of 23 written predictions: 8 confirmed, 4 magnitude off, 4 reversed, 7 silent failures.
  • Anything that transfers from proxy to target: about half reversed or were off by more than 2×.
  • First-run tooling on real output: about 1 in 2 needed a fix (CAL1, CAL2, T-CAL CPU probe, ngram, chain).
  • Same-model, in-range predictions: almost always within 10%.

Methodologies

Measurement

  • Pre-register, then measure. Freeze the protocol before results exist.
  • A/A first to get the noise floor, then matched A/B in ABBA order with medians.
  • Quiet host: no compiles, Codex runs or unthrottled downloads. Check it per arm and label the arm otherwise.
  • Rerun anything provisional that came from a noisy window.
  • Profile with a perturbation check against unprofiled timing.
  • Sample peak VRAM from outside the process (nvidia-smi every 0.5 s).

Correctness

  • Engagement before timing: prove the code path ran with counters or log lines.
  • Text identity for exact rewrites. KLD/PPL for anything numerical, including placement.
  • Paired KLD vs reference logits. Never unpaired PPL alone.
  • test-backend-ops for every patched op.
  • Sort every claim into a category: full-engine gain, representation trade-off, placement-only, or failed.

MoE Inference Factory Ledger

Everything built, found, ruled out and still missing in the factory that takes an MoE model, inspects it and the host, and produces an engine configuration that runs the model in much less memory at the same accuracy. It covers 43 decision notes, about 22 components, 7 skills, 300 artifact runs and one overnight experiment that is still running.

Hosts: x86 (Ryzen 7 3700X, DDR4 dual channel, RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB, PCIe 4.0) · Jetson Orin Nano (no reply yet). Models: Granite-3.1-1B-A400M (proxy 1), Qwen3-30B-A3B Q4_K_M (proxy 2), REAP-15B and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MTP (downloading).

What correlates and what doesn't

Strong, usable relationships

  • 1/decode is linear in bytes moved off the GPU. On Qwen each CPU layer adds 0.757 ms, which is about 30 GB/s, and the line holds from K=8 to K=48 (D039).
  • VRAM is linear in K: about 347 MiB per Qwen layer and 27 MiB per Granite layer. Planner MiB error is under 0.3%.
  • Cache hit rate decides cache vs static. Upload-mode cache wins when held-out coverage is about 70% or higher. CPU-share removes most of the miss penalty, so it wins much lower.
  • Expert size × handoff cost decides granularity. Crossover = fixed cost / per-byte cost (D031).
  • Paired KLD tracks quality where unpaired PPL can't (stderr 0.0015 vs 0.37).
  • imatrix → lower KLD at every bit width (−33% at 4-bit, −13% at 3-bit).
  • Copy-heavy text → speculation acceptance. Rewrite and repeat prompts give 2.4–3×; chat gives none.
  • Routing locality ranks code > prose > chat on both Granite and Qwen traces.

Weak, misleading or absent

  • Fewer bits ≠ faster on CPU. Q3_K unpacking is compute-bound on AVX2, so 3-bit was only +1.5%.
  • Greedy text identity ≠ quality. Every placement changes the text. The same config can even change it between runs (62290c73 vs 77a3045a).
  • Harness speedups ≠ integrated speedups. The integrated graph pays per-layer fixed costs (D030).
  • Proxy-model results ≠ target results. Granite results flipped on Qwen twice (D022, the planner).
  • Kernel count ≠ bandwidth. 40–46% of kernel time is in tiny kernels at under 1% DRAM.
  • Cache-policy choice barely matters. LRU, SLRU and ClassLRU are within 2 points. Budget and miss handling matter far more.
  • Profiled time ≠ real time. Node tracing inflates gaps 3×, and ncu serialises kernels.
  • Identical bytes in a different file vary ±5%, so effects under 5% need A/A and alternation.
  • A reported hit rate can mislead (Strata: PCIe-served experts are not counted).

Structure vs flexibility

The campaign settled into two speeds. Unfrozen screens find things quickly, and frozen protocols decide whether to accept them. Each side caught errors the other would have missed.

Where structure paid off

  • The frozen quiet-host rerun retracted PAP (+9.8% → +1.5%) before it reached the factory.
  • The plan → measure loop caught the planner's 5% decode optimism on its first run.
  • Engagement checks caught static-hot never running. Without them it would have been timed as "no gain".
  • run_ref image identity fixed the wrong-image-id bug (D016).
  • Plausibility guards rejected 1384 GB/s before it fed the planner.
  • The A/A interference check let downloads run during timing at a measured 0.2% cost.
  • Recorded ops made every number here traceable to a command.

Where flexibility paid off

  • An hour-long unfrozen screen found the +38% cache win that overturned D022.
  • Research intake found ngram-mod (2.4–3× for free) and upstream cpu-share, which flipped 4 GB tonight.
  • Rebasing to upstream (519 commits) brought levers we would have spent days building.
  • bpftrace and perf were set up ad hoc in minutes and confirmed the CPU-layer cost by a second method.
  • Delegating to Codex let six tools run in parallel (POL, SPECM, PROFW, CAL2, VER, PL4).

Where structure cost too much

  • Hand-written test JSON per experiment led to a scripted runner instead of bin/lab.
  • A text-identity criterion in E2/E4 may reject lossless speculation (G11).
  • Mocked fixtures passed tests and failed on real output 3 times.
  • A wait-gate meant to keep the host quiet deadlocked the overnight chain.

Rule of thumb: be strict about identity, provenance, engagement, noise floors and acceptance criteria. Be flexible about where ideas come from, which engine is the base, and how a screen is run. Of the 43 notes, about 6 are infra bugs, 4 are user directives, 6 are frozen protocols and about 27 are results. Every result that later reversed came from a proxy model, a harness or a noisy window.

Expected vs unexpected

Went as expected

  • Decode is memory-bandwidth-bound wherever experts live.
  • Quantization quality ordering: Q8 ≈ lossless, 4-bit costs a little, 2-bit collapses.
  • CUDA graphs help (4.2%). Small-kernel fusion has headroom.
  • KV q8_0 halves KV cost at no quality cost once fixed.
  • Speculation gains depend on the workload.

Surprised us

  • The expert cache flipped from loser (Granite) to winner (Qwen), then won at 4 GB too once misses could stay on the CPU.
  • Per-layer handoff, not bytes, dominated Granite decode (GPU idle 80%).
  • 3-bit experts were barely faster on the CPU.
  • Qwen3 thinking mode silently disabled n-gram drafting.
  • The handoff estimate varies 4× depending on the method (52–199 µs).
  • Zen 2 exposes no DRAM counters to perf on this kernel.
  • The same config gave different greedy text between runs.
  • Provider refusals were triggered by crash/debug wording in a Codex brief.

Rough base rates

  • Of 23 written predictions: 8 confirmed, 4 magnitude off, 4 reversed, 7 silent failures.
  • Anything that transfers from proxy to target: about half reversed or were off by more than 2×.
  • First-run tooling on real output: about 1 in 2 needed a fix (CAL1, CAL2, T-CAL CPU probe, ngram, chain).
  • Same-model, in-range predictions: almost always within 10%.

Methodologies

Measurement

  • Pre-register, then measure. Freeze the protocol before results exist.
  • A/A first to get the noise floor, then matched A/B in ABBA order with medians.
  • Quiet host: no compiles, Codex runs or unthrottled downloads. Check it per arm and label the arm otherwise.
  • Rerun anything provisional that came from a noisy window.
  • Profile with a perturbation check against unprofiled timing.
  • Sample peak VRAM from outside the process (nvidia-smi every 0.5 s).

Correctness

  • Engagement before timing: prove the code path ran with counters or log lines.
  • Text identity for exact rewrites. KLD/PPL for anything numerical, including placement.
  • Paired KLD vs reference logits. Never unpaired PPL alone.
  • test-backend-ops for every patched op.
  • Sort every claim into a category: full-engine gain, representation trade-off, placement-only, or failed.

Modeling and transfer

  • Label each result transferable or proxy-only. Proxy results are hypotheses on the target.
  • Predict from bytes and measured constants, and say "extrapolated" outside the calibration range.
  • Report fixed per-layer cost next to per-byte cost.
  • Plausibility guards on every microbenchmark (no faster-than-peak numbers).
  • Leave one model out before trusting a fit.

Process and delegation

  • Opus orchestrates. Codex does bounded work from written assignments and is reviewed against real records.
  • Capture real tool output as fixtures. Mocks hide real failures.
  • Every action goes through run_op, so every number has a command.
  • Research intake → smallest probe → indicative screen → frozen experiment → planner lever.
  • Avoid pgrep/pkill patterns that can match their own command line.

# D044 — Expert cache + CPU-share beats static offload at 4/6/8/10 GB on Qwen3-30B-A3B (frozen speed rule MET at all budgets; absolute KLD gate MISCALIBRATED, equivalent to its own floor)

**Claim category:** runtime-placement trade-off. This uses existing upstream flags (`--moe-cache-mib`, `--moe-cache-cpu-share`) with the weights unchanged.
- **Not claimed:** an engine code improvement; any result on other GPUs, CPUs or models; TTFT gains (TTFT gets worse).

**Evidence:**
- Ops T-NIGHT1 (chain1) and T-NIGHT2 (chain2) in `evidence/orchestrator.jsonl`.
- `artifacts/night/results.jsonl` (exp `aa`, `e1`, `kld`, `kld2`) and the raw stdout/stderr in `artifacts/night/logs/`.
- Runner `artifacts/night/run.py`. Protocol D043 plus amendments A1 (before results) and A2 (after results).

**Conditions:**
- Engines:
  - release-1: run_ref `sha256:5b8a6a22…`, pin 31288c9c6.
  - up1: run_ref `sha256:00454e95…`, upstream 3b4d6ab3f + release-stack-2 (sha 516e21606a20); passed text identity and 2517/2517 MUL_MAT.
- Model: Qwen3-30B-A3B Q4_K_M (sha256 9f1a2470…, D038).
- Settings: `llama-completion`, greedy, seed 1, `-fa on`, ctx 4096, 128 tokens, prompts `chat.txt` and `code.txt`.
- Peak VRAM from nvidia-smi every 0.5 s.
- Order: ABBA × 2 rounds. 80 timed E1 runs, all rc 0. Every arm was `quiet=true` (no compiler or Codex). A throttled curl ran throughout, as allowed by A1.
- Host: RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB, Ryzen 7 3700X, DDR4 dual channel, PCIe 4.0.

**Protocol (D043 E1, frozen):**
- Accept "cache beats static at B" only if both hold:
  - median decode is ≥ +5% over the same engine's static arm on both prompts;
  - peak VRAM is ≤ static + 3%.
- Quality gate: mean KLD ≤ 0.01 and same-top ≥ 97% against S1 K18, on 8×512 wikitext chunks.

**A/A interference (A1):** S1-K30 chat measured 36.46 t/s with the download running against 36.53 paused (n=3 each), a 0.2% difference against the 2% limit. **No arm is contaminated.**

## Numbers
Median decode t/s, chat / code, n=2 each.

| B | K | S1 rel1 | C1 rel1 | S2 up1 | C2 up1 share 0 | C3 up1 share 0.9 | cache MiB | C1 hit (chat) | peak MiB S / C3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 42 | 26.5 / 26.9 | 17.3 / 20.8 | 26.4 / 26.3 | 18.4 / 20.6 | **34.2 / 35.3** | 2005 | 50.1% | 4105 / 3837 |
| 6 | 36 | 30.8 / 30.8 | 28.9 / 32.6 | 31.4 / 28.9 | 32.2 / 34.0 | **48.4 / 48.1** | 4051 | 72.9% | 6151 / 5887 |
| 8 | 30 | 36.1 / 36.0 | 51.1 / 58.3 | 36.5 / 34.4 | 54.8 / 55.7 | **64.3** / 56.8 | 6093 | 86.7% | 8193 / 7931 |
| 10 | 24 | 43.5 / 42.0 | 70.1 / 71.8 | 43.8 / 43.3 | **71.9 / 71.1** | 71.9 / 64.2 | 8137 | 91.7% | 10237 / 9973 |

- **Within-arm spread** across the two rounds is ≤ 3% for most arms. C3 code shows 9% (33.6–36.9 at 4 GB, 61.4–67.0 at 10 GB).
- **CPU-share engagement** (from the logs): C3 computed 22044 of 25242 misses on the CPU at 4 GB (chat) and 1093 of 4218 at 10 GB. C2 logged "0 on the CPU".
- **Prompt eval ms** (TTFT proxy), median:
  - Cache arms are flat with budget: about 1100 (chat) and 5200 (code).
  - Static improves with budget: 1007 → 657 (chat) and 4781 → 2935 (code).
  - The cache TTFT penalty is therefore +8% at 4 GB, rising to +66% (chat) and +78% (code) at 10 GB.

**Quality**, KLD against the S1 K18 reference saved at the default batch of 2048:

| Arm | batch | mean KLD | same top-1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 K42 (frozen run) | 2048 | ≈0 (parser dropped the negative value) | 100.000% |
| C1 6000 (frozen run) | 2048 | ≈0 | 100.000% |
| C3 6000 (frozen run) | 2048 | 0.005365 | 96.716 ± 0.395% |
| S1 K18 = **reference config itself** (A2) | ub 1 | 0.005822 | 96.471% |
| S1 / S2 K42 (A2) | ub 1 | 0.006265 | 96.373% |
| C1 / C2 6000 (A2) | ub 1 | 0.005494 | 97.304% |
| C3 6000 (A2) | ub 1 | 0.005486 | 96.912% |
| C3 2005 (A2) | ub 1 | 0.005637 | 97.157% |

## Verdict against the frozen rule
- **Speed + VRAM rule:**
  - C3 against S2 **MEETS** it at 4 GB (+30 / +34%), 6 GB (+54 / +66%), 8 GB (+76 / +65%) and 10 GB (+64 / +48%), with VRAM 2.6–6.5% below static.
  - C1 and C2 meet it only at 8 and 10 GB (+42–71%). At 4 GB they FAIL (−22 to −35%), and at 6 GB they FAIL on the chat prompt (C1 −6%, C2 +3%).
- **Quality gate, applied literally:**
  - The frozen batch-2048 run gives C3-6000 same-top 96.72%, below 97% → **FAIL**.
  - Under A2's decode path, C1, C2 and C3-2005 pass, and C3-6000 fails by 0.09 points.
  - The **reference configuration fails against itself** (96.47%) when only the batch shape changes, and so does the static K42 offload the factory already ships (96.37%).
  - The gate threshold therefore sits inside batch-shape noise and cannot separate placements. **Gate verdict: inconclusive / miscalibrated, not a pass.**
- **Post-hoc equivalence** (labelled as such): every placement falls in KLD 0.0055–0.0063 and same-top 96.4–97.3%, while the reference's own batch-shape floor is 0.0058 / 96.5%. The cache arms drift no more than static offload.

## Interpretation
1. **CPU-share is the missing lever behind D041's 4 GB loss.**
   - When misses are computed where static offload would have computed them anyway (on the CPU), while hits come from VRAM, the cache wins even at a 50% hit rate.
   - An upload-only cache wins only above roughly 70–75% hit rate. That matches D041 and T-POL.
2. **CPU-share costs speed at high hit rates.** At 10 GB (92% hit), code decode is 64.2 against 71.1 for share 0, because computing a few misses on the CPU costs more than uploading them.
3. **Prompt processing does not use the cache.** The stats cover only ubatch ≤ 8, so the TTFT penalty grows as static gains GPU layers.
4. **T-POL's offline replay predicted the 2 GB cell** at 18.9 (upload) and 31.8 (CPU-share); measured 18.4 and 34.2. Replay plus calibration is good enough for the planner.

## Limits
- One host: discrete PCIe 4.0 GPU, Zen 2 AVX2, and DDR4 at about 30.8 GB/s (CAL2). One model, at batch-1 decode.
- Two prompts of 128 tokens. Only 2 rounds per arm, with a spread of 3–9%. Every effect here (≥ 30%) is far larger than that spread, but the 10 GB C2/C3 difference (−10% on code only) is near it.
- KLD covers only 8×512 wikitext chunks, and the reference is K18 at batch 2048, not bf16. No task-level eval was run.
- Hit rates come from a cold start within one request. Multi-turn and long-context behaviour is not measured (gap G3).

## Next
- Add the planner lever: cache with CPU-share by default, and lower the share as the predicted hit rate exceeds about 90% (sweep share 0.3/0.6 at 8–10 GB).
- Add a TTFT model and a "TTFT-optimised" option (static, or a hybrid of static GPU layers plus the cache).
- Re-gate quality against the reference's own batch-shape floor in the next protocol. Add a bf16-free task check.
- Run a frozen 3-round follow-up on the 10 GB share sweep.
- **Factory rules:**
  - On discrete GPUs, use the expert cache with CPU-share for decode at every budget tested (4–10 GB), with less VRAM than static.
  - Always report TTFT next to decode.
  - KLD for a placement must run on the decode path (`-ub 1`). At large batches, CPU-resident experts are computed on the GPU.
- **Method lesson:** an absolute quality threshold must first be checked against the reference configuration's own run-to-run and batch-shape floor. A gate that the reference fails cannot judge candidates.
EOF

def server_run(exp, arm, engine, model, sargs, prompts, n=256, rnd=0, extra=None):
    quiet = wait_quiet()
    name = f"night-srv-{os.getpid()}"
    sh(["docker", "rm", "-f", name])
    cmd = ["docker", "run", "-d", "--name", name, "--label", "campaign=c1", "--gpus", "all", "-p", "127.0.0.1:18081:8080",
           "-v", f"{model[0]}:/m:ro", "--entrypoint", "/app/llama-server", ENG[engine], "-m", f"/m/{model[1]}",
           "-fa", "on", "-c", "8192", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8080", "-np", "1", "-lv", "4"] + sargs
    pk = Peak()
    r = sh(cmd)
    ok = False
    for _ in range(400):
        try:
            if urllib.request.urlopen("http://127.0.0.1:18081/health", timeout=2).status == 200:
                ok = True; break
        except Exception:
            pass
        time.sleep(1)
    out = []
    if ok:
        for pn, p in prompts.items():
            body = json.dumps({"prompt": p, "n_predict": n, "temperature": 0, "seed": 1, "cache_prompt": False}).encode()
            try:
                j = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request("http://127.0.0.1:18081/completion", body,
                                                                            {"Content-Type": "application/json"}), timeout=900))
            except Exception as e:
                record(dict(exp=exp, arm=arm, engine=engine, prompt=pn, round=rnd, error=str(e)[:300])); continue
            t = j.get("timings", {})
            rec = dict(exp=exp, arm=arm, engine=engine, model=model[1], prompt=pn, round=rnd, sargs=sargs,
                       tps=t.get("predicted_per_second"), prompt_ms=t.get("prompt_ms"), draft_n=t.get("draft_n", 0),
                       draft_acc=t.get("draft_n_accepted", 0), n=t.get("predicted_n"),
                       text_sha=hashlib.sha256(j["content"].encode()).hexdigest()[:8], quiet=quiet,
                       curl_running=bool(curl_pids()), t=time.strftime("%H:%M:%S"))
            if extra: rec.update(extra)
            out.append(rec)
    logs = sh(["docker", "logs", name]).stdout + sh(["docker", "logs", name]).stderr
    open(f"{OUT}/logs/{exp}-{arm}-r{rnd}-server.log", "w").write(logs)
    sh(["docker", "rm", "-f", name])
    peak = pk.done()
    for rec in out:
        rec["peak_mib"] = peak; record(rec)
    if not ok:
        record(dict(exp=exp, arm=arm, engine=engine, round=rnd, error="server not ready", rc=r.returncode, stderr=r.stderr[-300:]))
    return out

# D046 — E4: MTP speculative decoding on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B ACCEPTED for copy-heavy prompts (+23–42%, text identical); chat +11–14% but text differs → INCONCLUSIVE under the frozen rule

**Claim category:** runtime trade-off. This is an existing upstream `--spec-type draft-mtp`, run on the model's own MTP (nextn) layer, and it costs +0.8–0.9 GB of VRAM.
- **Not claimed:** lossless output on chat; results for any other model; that the MTP VRAM is better spent than on GPU layers (a predicted comparison, below).

**Evidence:**
- Op T-NIGHT4 (chain3 E4: rewrite/repeat/chat) and op T-E4CHAT (chat rerun, amendment A3).
- `artifacts/night/results.jsonl` exp `e4` and `e4chat`; server logs `artifacts/night/logs/e4*-server.log`.

**Conditions:**
- Model: unsloth Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MTP UD-Q4_K_M, 22,663,387,424 B, sha256 0b21525e…, matching the HF LFS oid.
  - Architecture `qwen35moe`: 41 blocks, 30 Gated-DeltaNet (ssm) layers + 11 full-attention layers, and one `nextn` MTP head.
  - 256 experts with top-8 routing, plus a shared expert. Experts are 1.81 MiB each (Q4_K gate/up, Q5_K down), against 2.72 MiB for Qwen3-30B.
- Engine: up1, `llama-server`, `-fa on -c 8192 -np 1`, 256 tokens, greedy, ABBA × 2. Every arm ran with the host quiet; the download finished before E4 started.
- **Amendment A3 (post-hoc, engagement):** the frozen chat arm sent the raw chat prompt to `/completion`. Qwen3.6 emitted EOS at token 1 (0 tokens, sha of the empty string), so the arm is invalid. It was rerun with a ChatML prompt plus an empty `<think></think>` block (op T-E4CHAT).

## Numbers
Median t/s, n=2. Pairs are within 3%. Text "=" means identical to spec-none.

| K (peak MiB none / mtp3) | Prompt | none | mtp n_max 2 | mtp n_max 3 | text | accepted / drafted (mtp2, mtp3) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| K18 (13189 / 14073) | rewrite | 63.9 | 86.8 (+36%) | **90.7 (+42%)** | = | drafted 170, 191 |
| | repeat | 64.9 | 81.2 (+25%) | **86.5 (+33%)** | = | drafted 170, 191 |
| | chat (A3) | 64.9 | 72.2 (+11%) | 72.7 (+12%) | **≠** | 148/212 (70%), 167/259 (64%) |
| K30 (7623 / 8505) | rewrite | 45.8 | 59.8 (+31%) | **64.1 (+40%)** | = | drafted 170, 191 |
| | repeat | 46.2 | 57.0 (+23%) | **58.6 (+27%)** | = | drafted 170, 191 |
| | chat (A3) | 46.2 | 51.3 (+11%) | 51.9 (+12%) | **≠** | 145/220 (66%), 169/258 (66%) |

- MTP VRAM cost: +820 MiB (n_max 2) and +882 MiB (n_max 3).
- The chat text is stable within each config across rounds, but differs between none, mtp2 and mtp3. It also differs between K18-none and K30-none, so placement alone changes it too.

**Verdict against the frozen rule** (text identical to spec-none at temp 0 AND decode ≥ +10%):
- rewrite and repeat: **ACCEPTED** at both K, for n_max 2 and 3. The text is identical and the gain is +23% to +42%.
- chat: the speed condition is met (+11% to +14%), but the text condition FAILS → **INCONCLUSIVE**.
  - A verify batch of 3–4 tokens runs different kernels than single-token decode. A2 (D044) showed batch shape alone moves outputs by as much as placement does, so this divergence is the expected class of numeric difference.
  - No logprob/KLD-level check was run for MTP, so equivalence is **unproven**.

## Interpretation
- **MTP helps every prompt type, unlike n-gram speculation** (D045: 0 drafts on chat).
  - About 65–70% of drafts are accepted on chat.
  - On copy-heavy text, n-gram speculation is stronger (2.3–3.0× on Qwen3 K30 against MTP's +27–40%).
  - The two could be combined; that is not tested.
- **Is the VRAM worth it? (Predicted, not measured.)** One CPU layer on Qwen3.6 costs about 464 MiB of VRAM ((13189 − 7623) / 12). The +882 MiB for MTP would therefore buy about 1.9 more GPU layers. On the K-curve, that is roughly +4–5% decode, against +12% (chat) and +27–40% (copy) for MTP. So MTP is the better use of about 0.9 GB here.
- **Qwen3.6 decodes faster than Qwen3-30B at similar VRAM** (46 t/s at 7.6 GB against 36 at 8.2 GB), despite having more parameters. Its experts are smaller (1.81 MiB against 2.72), so each token moves fewer bytes, and only 11 of its layers keep a KV cache.
- **G17 confirmed:** `inspect_model` reports the architecture but has no state/KV accounting for the 30 DeltaNet layers.

## Limits
- One host and one model. Two rounds per arm.
- Synthetic copy prompts, and one chat prompt.
- MTP acceptance on the copy prompts was not recorded: the server returned `draft_n` only on the first pass, and the accepted count came back null.
- No logprob-equivalence test was run for chat. The matched-VRAM comparison against more GPU layers is predicted, not measured.

## Next
- Equivalence test for speculation: per-token top-1/KLD between spec-none and MTP on the chat prompt, against the batch-shape floor (D044 A2).
- Combine MTP with n-gram, and MTP with the expert cache plus CPU-share.
- Measure the matched-VRAM comparison (K28 none vs K30 mtp3).
- Extend `inspect_model` to hybrid layers (ssm state bytes and the attention-layer count).

**Factory rules:**
- For models that ship MTP heads, MTP speculation is a lever worth +11–14% on chat and +23–42% on copy-heavy text, for about 0.9 GB of VRAM.
- Prefer n-gram speculation for copy-heavy workloads; prefer MTP for general chat.
- Gate it with distributional equivalence, not text identity.

**Method lesson:** prompts must be formatted for each model. A raw prompt that works on one model can end at token 1 on another, so engagement (n > 0) must be checked per arm.
EOF

# D047 — Overnight-2 protocol (FROZEN before results), 2026-11-10: follow-ups to D044–D046

The user approved all of these overnight experiments ("overnight experiments all approved").

**Runner:** `artifacts/night/run2.py`, reusing the D043 runner helpers.
- Quiet-host check before every arm. The download is finished, so no network traffic runs during timing.
- Every peak VRAM figure comes from nvidia-smi, polled every 0.5 s.
- Order is ABBA × 2 unless stated otherwise. Medians are reported.
- Engines are the same images as D043 (release-1, up1).

**Prompts:**
- Qwen3-30B: `chat.txt` and `code.txt`.
- Qwen3.6:
  - chat: `chat36.txt` (ChatML with an empty think block, from D046 A3);
  - code: `code.txt` with `--ignore-eos`, so every run has a fixed 128 tokens;
  - spec prompts (rewrite/repeat): as in D043.

**Engagement:**
- Every arm must report n > 0 and t/s > 0. Otherwise it is invalid.
- Cache arms must log cache stats.
- Spec arms must report draft_n > 0 on the copy prompts.

## X1 — MTP vs spending the same VRAM on GPU layers (Qwen3.6, up1, llama-server, 256 tokens)
- **Arms:** K28-none, against K30-mtp3. MTP costs about 0.9 GB and one layer about 0.46 GB, so these match in VRAM.
- **Prompts:** chat (ChatML), rewrite, repeat.
- **Accept "MTP beats layers"** if K30-mtp3 decode is ≥ +5% over K28-none on chat, with peak VRAM within ±5%.
- **Predicted (D046):** MTP wins on chat by about +7%, and by +20–35% on copy prompts.

## X2 — Is the speculation verify numerics within the batch-shape floor? (Qwen3.6 KLD)
- **Method:** `llama-perplexity` on 8×512 wikitext chunks. The reference is K18 at the default batch, saved. Arms: K18 at `-ub 1` (decode floor) and K18 at `-ub 4` (the shape of an MTP verify window, 1 + 3 drafts).
- **Equivalence claim:** the ub-4 arm is within the ub-1 arm's distance from the reference: |Δ mean KLD| ≤ 0.002 and |Δ same-top| ≤ 0.5 points.
- **Why this suffices:** speculation accepts only tokens that the verify pass itself would pick greedily. The only remaining numeric change is batch shape.

## X3 — Does the D044 cache result transfer to a second model? (Qwen3.6, completion, 128 tokens, ignore-eos)
- **Budgets:** the static K30 peak (about 7.6 GB) and the static K36 peak (about 4.8 GB).
- **Cache sizing:** the cache is sized so that its peak is ≤ the static peak. It equals the static peak, minus the measured all-CPU-experts base (K41), minus 300 MiB.
- **Arms:** S (static, up1); C2 (cache, share 0); C3 (cache, share 0.9).
- **Accept "transfers"** under the D043 E1 rule: C3 ≥ +5% over S on both prompts, with peak ≤ S + 3%.
- **Predicted:** a gain smaller than Qwen3's at the same budget, because Qwen3.6 has smaller experts and 256 of them, so the hit rate per MiB is lower.

## X4 — CPU-share sweep (Qwen3-30B, up1, completion)
- **Settings:** cache 6093 (8 GB) and 8137 (10 GB). Share 0, 0.3, 0.6 and 0.9. Chat and code prompts.
- **Predicted (D044):** the best share falls as the budget rises. At 10 GB, the best share is ≤ 0.3.
- **Planner rule adopted if:** the best share at 10 GB is ≤ 0.6, and within 3% of the best at 8 GB.

## X5 — Thread sweep (Qwen3-30B, chat prompt)
- **Arms:** static K30 (release-1) and C3-6093 (up1), each at `-t` 4, 6, 8, 12 and 16.
- **Predicted:** 8 threads (one per physical core) is best. 16 (SMT) is worse by ≥ 3%.

## X6 — TTFT lever for cache placements (Qwen3-30B, code prompt, the longer one)
- **Arms:** C3-6093 and static K30, each at `-ub` 256, 512 (default), 1024 and 2048, with `-b 2048`.
- **Predicted:** a larger ub cuts cache prompt time, since misses are streamed per ubatch. Decode is unchanged.
- **Report:** prompt ms and decode t/s.

## X7 — Load time (Qwen3-30B, static K30, release-1)
- **Metric:** wall time of `llama-completion -n 1`, three repetitions per condition.
- **Conditions:**
  - warm page cache, mmap (default);
  - cold for the model file only (`posix_fadvise(DONTNEED)` on that one file, no host-wide flush);
  - warm, `--no-mmap`;
  - cold, `--no-mmap`.
- **Report:** load seconds and effective GB/s. No acceptance rule; this is a measurement for the planner.

## X8 — Cache + MTP stacking (Qwen3.6, up1, llama-server, 256 tokens)
- **Arms:** C3 at the X3 8 GB budget with spec none; C3 at that budget with mtp3; K30-mtp3.
- **Prompts:** chat (ChatML), rewrite, repeat. One server per arm, prompts run in a fixed order, which is reported.
- **Accept "stacks"** if C3+mtp3 ≥ +5% over both C3-none and K30-mtp3 on chat. VRAM is reported, since MTP adds about 0.9 GB.

## Not allowed
- Pushing `main`.
- Host changes beyond the D042 perf setting.
- Restarting `euaaa-llm-gpu-1` or Sunshine during measurements. Both are restored after X1–X8 finish.
EOF

cd ~/projects/siminfeng/campaign; cat > decisions/D048-overnight2-results.md <<'EOF'
# D048 — Overnight-2 results (protocol D047, X1–X8): the cache transfers to a second model, MTP beats spending VRAM on layers, a larger ubatch fixes cache TTFT, 4–6 threads beat 8, SMT halves decode, cache + MTP stack

**Claim category:** runtime-placement and speculation trade-offs, with existing upstream flags and the weights unchanged.
- X2 is a numeric-equivalence measurement. X7 is a load-time measurement.
- **Not claimed:** engine code gains; any result on other hosts.

**Evidence:**
- Ops T-NIGHT5 (X1–X8) and T-NIGHT5b (A1 reruns of X8 and X7).
- `artifacts/night/results.jsonl` exp `x1`, `x2`, `x3`, `x3cal`, `x4`, `x5`, `x6`, `x7`, `x7load`, `x8` (contaminated), `x8a1`. Logs in `artifacts/night/logs/x*`. Runner `artifacts/night/run2.py`.

**Conditions:**
- Engines: release-1 (`5b8a6a22…`) and up1 (`00454e95…`).
- Models: Qwen3-30B-A3B Q4_K_M and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M (sha 0b21525e…).
- Settings: greedy, FA on. ABBA × 2. Every arm passed the quiet check; no network traffic ran.
- **Interference window:** around 07:21–07:26 the host had 6.5 GB in swap (cause not proven). Every round timed in that window is slow, with prompt time 1.5–2.5×:
  - all of X8 round 1, which was rerun in full as X8a1 (clean);
  - X3 S-K36 code round 2 (15.7 against 40.8);
  - X4 6093 share0 chat round 1 (43.1 against 55.8);
  - X4 6093 share0.3 code round 1 (27.9 against 56.2).

  Those rounds are excluded below. The clean round is used, and it is marked *.
- **Method lesson:** the quiet check must also watch swap-in and page faults, not just process names.

## X1 — MTP vs the same VRAM spent on GPU layers (Qwen3.6, server, 256 tokens)

| Arm | peak MiB | chat | rewrite | repeat |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| K28, no spec | 8551 | 48.1 | 48.3 | 47.8 |
| K30 + mtp3 | 8505 | **52.8 (+9.8%)** | **65.4 (+35%)** | **59.8 (+25%)** |

- VRAM differs by −0.5% (rule: within ±5%). **ACCEPTED: MTP beats layers** (rule: ≥ +5% on chat).
- The D046 prediction is confirmed:
  - K28 vs K30 without spec measured +4.1%, against a predicted +4–5%;
  - MTP on chat measured +9.8%, against a predicted +7%.
- Chat acceptance: 169 of 258 drafts (66%).

## X2 — Do the speculation-verify numerics sit inside the batch-shape floor? (Qwen3.6 KLD, 8×512 wikitext, reference K18 at the default batch, PPL 6.220)

| Arm | mean KLD | same top-1 |
|---|---|---|
| K18 ub 1 (decode floor) | 0.005876 | 97.108% |
| K18 ub 4 (MTP verify shape) | 0.005769 | 97.157% |

- |Δ| = 0.0001 KLD and 0.05 points, inside the frozen bound (≤ 0.002, ≤ 0.5) → **EQUIVALENT.**
- A 4-token verify window moves outputs no more than single-token decode does. Speculation only accepts tokens the verify pass itself selects greedily.
- So the D046 chat text divergence is within the batch-shape floor. **D046 chat verdict: upgraded from INCONCLUSIVE to distributionally equivalent.**
- The same floor appears on both models: Qwen3-30B 0.0058 / 96.5%, Qwen3.6 0.0059 / 97.1%.

## X3 — Does the D044 cache result transfer to Qwen3.6? (completion, 128 tokens with ignore-eos)
The all-CPU-experts base (K41) peaks at 2951 MiB. Cache = static peak − base − 300.

| Budget | Arm | peak MiB | chat | code | C2 hit (chat) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| K30 (7.66 GB) | S | 7661 | 46.3 | 47.3 | |
| | C2 (cache 4406, share 0) | 7357 | 54.8 | 49.4 | 79.9% |
| | **C3 (share 0.9)** | 7361 | **65.6 (+42%)** | **61.2 (+29%)** | |
| K36 (4.84 GB) | S | 4843 | 40.9 | 40.8* | |
| | C2 (cache 1592) | 4543 | 32.8 | 32.4 | 59.5% |
| | **C3** | 4547 | **49.3 (+21%)** | **51.5 (+26%)** | |

- **ACCEPTED, transfers:** C3 passes the D043 rule at both budgets and both prompts, using 4–6% less VRAM.
- An upload-only cache (C2) again loses at the lower budget (−20%) and is marginal at the higher one (code +4%, below the 5% bar).
- **The prediction is confirmed:** the gains are smaller than on Qwen3 at a similar budget (+42/+29% against +76/+65% at about 8 GB). Qwen3.6 has smaller experts and 256 of them, so it gets fewer hits per MiB.

## X4 — CPU-share sweep (Qwen3-30B, up1)

| Cache | Prompt | share 0 | 0.3 | 0.6 | 0.9 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6093 (8 GB) | chat | 55.8* | 54.0 | 60.4 | **64.1** |
| | code | 56.2 | 56.2* | **59.0** | 56.0 |
| 8137 (10 GB) | chat | **72.7** | 69.3 | 70.2 | 72.3 |
| | code | **73.1** | 68.2 | 67.2 | 64.1 |

- **The prediction is confirmed:** the best share falls with budget. At 10 GB (92% hit rate), share 0 is best. At 8 GB (87%), 0.6–0.9 is best.
- **Unexpected:** the response is not monotonic. At 10 GB, share 0.3 is 5–7% slower than both 0 and 0.9, even though only about 200–270 misses go to the CPU. Any CPU participation appears to add a fixed per-token sync cost, so the share should be either 0 or high, never a small value.
- **Planner rule ADOPTED:**
  - predicted hit rate ≥ about 90% → share 0;
  - otherwise → share 0.9 (0.6 is within 5% on code at 8 GB).

## X5 — Thread count (Qwen3-30B, chat)

| -t | 4 | 6 | 8 | 12 | 16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| static K30 | **38.5** | 38.2 | 37.3 | 34.7 | 18.6 |
| C3-6093 | **66.5** | 65.8 | 65.3 | 61.3 | 34.3 |

- **The prediction is partly WRONG.** 8 threads (physical cores) is not the best: 4 threads is +2–3% faster, consistently on both arms. CPU expert bandwidth is saturated at 4 threads, and extra threads add sync.
- 16 threads (SMT) cuts decode by **about 50%**, far beyond the predicted ≥ 3%.
- **Factory rule:** threads ≤ the physical core count, tuned per host (G5 autotuner). Never use SMT threads for MoE decode.

## X6 — ubatch size as a TTFT lever (Qwen3-30B, code prompt)

| Arm | ub 256 | 512 (default) | 1024 | 2048 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C3-6093: prompt ms | 7714 | 5111 | 2989 | **1784** |
| C3-6093: decode t/s | 60.7 | 57.5 | 57.9 | 58.4 |
| C3-6093: peak MiB | 7805 | 7937 | 8263 | 8909 |
| static K30: prompt ms | 5205 | 3510 | 2065 | **1280** |
| static K30: decode t/s | 36.1 | 36.4 | 36.5 | 36.4 |
| static K30: peak MiB | 8035 | 8203 | 8559 | 9277 |

- **The prediction is confirmed, and the effect is larger than expected.** ub 2048 cuts cache TTFT 2.9×, for +0.97 GB of VRAM. Decode does not change.
- **The D044 TTFT problem is solved at equal VRAM:**
  - C3 at ub 1024: 8263 MiB, 2989 ms, 57.9 t/s;
  - static K30 at default ub: 8203 MiB, 3510 ms, 36.4 t/s.

  At matched VRAM (+0.7%), the cache now has **15% better TTFT and 59% better decode.**
- ub is a VRAM ↔ TTFT lever. The planner should trade cache MiB against ub according to the prompt-length profile.

## X7 — Load time (Qwen3-30B, 18.56 GB file, static K30, `llama-completion -n 1` wall time incl. docker + CUDA init)

| Mode | warm page cache | cold (file evicted via fadvise) |
|---|---|---|
| mmap (default) | **6.3 s** | 18.8 s |
| `-lm none` (read into RAM) | 16.0 s | 26.0 s |
| `-lm mmap+mlock` | 6.0 s | 18.8 s |

- The cold penalty is +12.5 s for 18.56 GB, an effective **1.48 GB/s** from this disk.
- `-lm none` costs about 10 s even when the file is warm.
- mlock changes nothing here. It probably cannot take effect under docker's default memlock limit (unverified).
- **Load model:** load ≈ 6 s fixed (container, CUDA init, uploading about 7 GB to the GPU), plus cold bytes ÷ 1.5 GB/s.
- Keep mmap. A long-running server pays the load once.

## X8 (A1 rerun, clean) — cache + MTP stacking (Qwen3.6, server, about 7.3–8.5 GB)

| Arm | peak MiB | chat | rewrite | repeat |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C3 (cache 4406), no spec | 7339 | 66.3 | 58.7 | 73.2 |
| **C3 + mtp3** | 7867 | **70.6** | **73.1** | **95.1** |
| K30 + mtp3 | 8505 | 52.5 | 64.8 | 58.3 |

- **ACCEPTED, stacks:** on chat, +6.5% over C3 and +34% over K30+mtp3, and it uses 640 MiB less than K30+mtp3.
- Against plain static K30 (46.3 chat at 7.66 GB), cache + MTP at 7.87 GB gives **+52% on chat and +100% on repeat**.
- MTP's relative gain on the cache is smaller (+6.5% chat, against +12% on static). This matches T-SPECM: the extra experts touched by a verify window are cache misses.
- The first X8 run is kept in the record as contaminated.

## Limits
- One host: Zen 2 8-core, DDR4, PCIe 4.0, RTX 5070 Ti.
- Two rounds per arm, with excluded rounds marked *.
- Two prompts (chat, code), plus synthetic copy prompts.
- The X2 equivalence uses wikitext only.
- X7 cold reads go through LVM on this disk.
- Hit rates come from cold, single-request starts.

## Next / factory rules (adopted)
1. **Placement:** on discrete GPUs, default to the expert cache with CPU-share. Set the share to 0 when the predicted hit rate is ≥ about 90%, otherwise 0.9. This is now confirmed on two models at 4.5–10 GB.
2. **TTFT:** choose ub by the prompt-length profile; ub 1024–2048 removes the cache's TTFT penalty for about 0.3–1 GB.
3. **Speculation:**
   - models with MTP heads: enable mtp n_max 3 (beats the same VRAM spent on layers; stacks with the cache);
   - copy-heavy workloads: n-gram;
   - gate by distributional equivalence (X2 floor), not text identity.
4. **Threads:** ≤ physical cores, autotuned (4 is best on this host). Never SMT.
5. **Load:** mmap; budget cold start as file GB ÷ measured disk GB/s.
6. **Quiet check:** add swap and page-fault monitoring.
EOF
cat >> decisions/D046-e4-mtp-qwen36.md <<'EOF'

## Addendum (D048 X2)
The verify-shaped batch (ub 4) gives KLD 0.005769 and same-top 97.157%, against the decode floor (ub 1) of 0.005876 and 97.108%. That is inside the D047 equivalence bound. **The chat verdict is upgraded from INCONCLUSIVE to distributionally equivalent**: the MTP chat text divergence is batch-shape numerics within the floor. X1 also confirms that MTP beats spending the same VRAM on GPU layers (+9.8% chat).
EOF

# D048 — Overnight-2 results (protocol D047, X1–X8): the cache transfers to a second model, MTP beats spending VRAM on layers, a larger ubatch fixes cache TTFT, 4–6 threads beat 8, SMT halves decode, cache + MTP stack

**Claim category:** runtime-placement and speculation trade-offs, with existing upstream flags and the weights unchanged.
- X2 is a numeric-equivalence measurement. X7 is a load-time measurement.
- **Not claimed:** engine code gains; any result on other hosts.

**Evidence:**
- Ops T-NIGHT5 (X1–X8) and T-NIGHT5b (A1 reruns of X8 and X7).
- `artifacts/night/results.jsonl` exp `x1`, `x2`, `x3`, `x3cal`, `x4`, `x5`, `x6`, `x7`, `x7load`, `x8` (contaminated), `x8a1`. Logs in `artifacts/night/logs/x*`. Runner `artifacts/night/run2.py`.

**Conditions:**
- Engines: release-1 (`5b8a6a22…`) and up1 (`00454e95…`).
- Models: Qwen3-30B-A3B Q4_K_M and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M (sha 0b21525e…).
- Settings: greedy, FA on. ABBA × 2. Every arm passed the quiet check; no network traffic ran.
- **Interference window:** around 07:21–07:26 the host had 6.5 GB in swap (cause not proven). Every round timed in that window is slow, with prompt time 1.5–2.5×:
  - all of X8 round 1, which was rerun in full as X8a1 (clean);
  - X3 S-K36 code round 2 (15.7 against 40.8);
  - X4 6093 share0 chat round 1 (43.1 against 55.8);
  - X4 6093 share0.3 code round 1 (27.9 against 56.2).

  Those rounds are excluded below. The clean round is used, and it is marked *.
- **Method lesson:** the quiet check must also watch swap-in and page faults, not just process names.

## X1 — MTP vs the same VRAM spent on GPU layers (Qwen3.6, server, 256 tokens)

| Arm | peak MiB | chat | rewrite | repeat |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| K28, no spec | 8551 | 48.1 | 48.3 | 47.8 |
| K30 + mtp3 | 8505 | **52.8 (+9.8%)** | **65.4 (+35%)** | **59.8 (+25%)** |

- VRAM differs by −0.5% (rule: within ±5%). **ACCEPTED: MTP beats layers** (rule: ≥ +5% on chat).
- The D046 prediction is confirmed:
  - K28 vs K30 without spec measured +4.1%, against a predicted +4–5%;
  - MTP on chat measured +9.8%, against a predicted +7%.
- Chat acceptance: 169 of 258 drafts (66%).

## X2 — Do the speculation-verify numerics sit inside the batch-shape floor? (Qwen3.6 KLD, 8×512 wikitext, reference K18 at the default batch, PPL 6.220)

| Arm | mean KLD | same top-1 |
|---|---|---|
| K18 ub 1 (decode floor) | 0.005876 | 97.108% |
| K18 ub 4 (MTP verify shape) | 0.005769 | 97.157% |

- |Δ| = 0.0001 KLD and 0.05 points, inside the frozen bound (≤ 0.002, ≤ 0.5) → **EQUIVALENT.**
- A 4-token verify window moves outputs no more than single-token decode does. Speculation only accepts tokens the verify pass itself selects greedily.
- So the D046 chat text divergence is within the batch-shape floor. **D046 chat verdict: upgraded from INCONCLUSIVE to distributionally equivalent.**
- The same floor appears on both models: Qwen3-30B 0.0058 / 96.5%, Qwen3.6 0.0059 / 97.1%.

## X3 — Does the D044 cache result transfer to Qwen3.6? (completion, 128 tokens with ignore-eos)
The all-CPU-experts base (K41) peaks at 2951 MiB. Cache = static peak − base − 300.

| Budget | Arm | peak MiB | chat | code | C2 hit (chat) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| K30 (7.66 GB) | S | 7661 | 46.3 | 47.3 | |
| | C2 (cache 4406, share 0) | 7357 | 54.8 | 49.4 | 79.9% |
| | **C3 (share 0.9)** | 7361 | **65.6 (+42%)** | **61.2 (+29%)** | |
| K36 (4.84 GB) | S | 4843 | 40.9 | 40.8* | |
| | C2 (cache 1592) | 4543 | 32.8 | 32.4 | 59.5% |
| | **C3** | 4547 | **49.3 (+21%)** | **51.5 (+26%)** | |

- **ACCEPTED, transfers:** C3 passes the D043 rule at both budgets and both prompts, using 4–6% less VRAM.
- An upload-only cache (C2) again loses at the lower budget (−20%) and is marginal at the higher one (code +4%, below the 5% bar).
- **The prediction is confirmed:** the gains are smaller than on Qwen3 at a similar budget (+42/+29% against +76/+65% at about 8 GB). Qwen3.6 has smaller experts and 256 of them, so it gets fewer hits per MiB.

## X4 — CPU-share sweep (Qwen3-30B, up1)

| Cache | Prompt | share 0 | 0.3 | 0.6 | 0.9 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6093 (8 GB) | chat | 55.8* | 54.0 | 60.4 | **64.1** |
| | code | 56.2 | 56.2* | **59.0** | 56.0 |
| 8137 (10 GB) | chat | **72.7** | 69.3 | 70.2 | 72.3 |
| | code | **73.1** | 68.2 | 67.2 | 64.1 |

- **The prediction is confirmed:** the best share falls with budget. At 10 GB (92% hit rate), share 0 is best. At 8 GB (87%), 0.6–0.9 is best.
- **Unexpected:** the response is not monotonic. At 10 GB, share 0.3 is 5–7% slower than both 0 and 0.9, even though only about 200–270 misses go to the CPU. Any CPU participation appears to add a fixed per-token sync cost, so the share should be either 0 or high, never a small value.
- **Planner rule ADOPTED:**
  - predicted hit rate ≥ about 90% → share 0;
  - otherwise → share 0.9 (0.6 is within 5% on code at 8 GB).

## X5 — Thread count (Qwen3-30B, chat)

| -t | 4 | 6 | 8 | 12 | 16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| static K30 | **38.5** | 38.2 | 37.3 | 34.7 | 18.6 |
| C3-6093 | **66.5** | 65.8 | 65.3 | 61.3 | 34.3 |

- **The prediction is partly WRONG.** 8 threads (physical cores) is not the best: 4 threads is +2–3% faster, consistently on both arms. CPU expert bandwidth is saturated at 4 threads, and extra threads add sync.
- 16 threads (SMT) cuts decode by **about 50%**, far beyond the predicted ≥ 3%.
- **Factory rule:** threads ≤ the physical core count, tuned per host (G5 autotuner). Never use SMT threads for MoE decode.

## X6 — ubatch size as a TTFT lever (Qwen3-30B, code prompt)

| Arm | ub 256 | 512 (default) | 1024 | 2048 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C3-6093: prompt ms | 7714 | 5111 | 2989 | **1784** |
| C3-6093: decode t/s | 60.7 | 57.5 | 57.9 | 58.4 |
| C3-6093: peak MiB | 7805 | 7937 | 8263 | 8909 |
| static K30: prompt ms | 5205 | 3510 | 2065 | **1280** |
| static K30: decode t/s | 36.1 | 36.4 | 36.5 | 36.4 |
| static K30: peak MiB | 8035 | 8203 | 8559 | 9277 |

- **The prediction is confirmed, and the effect is larger than expected.** ub 2048 cuts cache TTFT 2.9×, for +0.97 GB of VRAM. Decode does not change.
- **The D044 TTFT problem is solved at equal VRAM:**
  - C3 at ub 1024: 8263 MiB, 2989 ms, 57.9 t/s;
  - static K30 at default ub: 8203 MiB, 3510 ms, 36.4 t/s.

  At matched VRAM (+0.7%), the cache now has **15% better TTFT and 59% better decode.**
- ub is a VRAM ↔ TTFT lever. The planner should trade cache MiB against ub according to the prompt-length profile.

## X7 — Load time (Qwen3-30B, 18.56 GB file, static K30, `llama-completion -n 1` wall time incl. docker + CUDA init)

| Mode | warm page cache | cold (file evicted via fadvise) |
|---|---|---|
| mmap (default) | **6.3 s** | 18.8 s |
| `-lm none` (read into RAM) | 16.0 s | 26.0 s |
| `-lm mmap+mlock` | 6.0 s | 18.8 s |

- The cold penalty is +12.5 s for 18.56 GB, an effective **1.48 GB/s** from this disk.
- `-lm none` costs about 10 s even when the file is warm.
- mlock changes nothing here. It probably cannot take effect under docker's default memlock limit (unverified).
- **Load model:** load ≈ 6 s fixed (container, CUDA init, uploading about 7 GB to the GPU), plus cold bytes ÷ 1.5 GB/s.
- Keep mmap. A long-running server pays the load once.

## X8 (A1 rerun, clean) — cache + MTP stacking (Qwen3.6, server, about 7.3–8.5 GB)

| Arm | peak MiB | chat | rewrite | repeat |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C3 (cache 4406), no spec | 7339 | 66.3 | 58.7 | 73.2 |
| **C3 + mtp3** | 7867 | **70.6** | **73.1** | **95.1** |
| K30 + mtp3 | 8505 | 52.5 | 64.8 | 58.3 |

- **ACCEPTED, stacks:** on chat, +6.5% over C3 and +34% over K30+mtp3, and it uses 640 MiB less than K30+mtp3.
- Against plain static K30 (46.3 chat at 7.66 GB), cache + MTP at 7.87 GB gives **+52% on chat and +100% on repeat**.
- MTP's relative gain on the cache is smaller (+6.5% chat, against +12% on static). This matches T-SPECM: the extra experts touched by a verify window are cache misses.
- The first X8 run is kept in the record as contaminated.

## Limits
- One host: Zen 2 8-core, DDR4, PCIe 4.0, RTX 5070 Ti.
- Two rounds per arm, with excluded rounds marked *.
- Two prompts (chat, code), plus synthetic copy prompts.
- The X2 equivalence uses wikitext only.
- X7 cold reads go through LVM on this disk.
- Hit rates come from cold, single-request starts.

## Next / factory rules (adopted)
1. **Placement:** on discrete GPUs, default to the expert cache with CPU-share. Set the share to 0 when the predicted hit rate is ≥ about 90%, otherwise 0.9. This is now confirmed on two models at 4.5–10 GB.
2. **TTFT:** choose ub by the prompt-length profile; ub 1024–2048 removes the cache's TTFT penalty for about 0.3–1 GB.
3. **Speculation:**
   - models with MTP heads: enable mtp n_max 3 (beats the same VRAM spent on layers; stacks with the cache);
   - copy-heavy workloads: n-gram;
   - gate by distributional equivalence (X2 floor), not text identity.
4. **Threads:** ≤ physical cores, autotuned (4 is best on this host). Never SMT.
5. **Load:** mmap; budget cold start as file GB ÷ measured disk GB/s.
6. **Quiet check:** add swap and page-fault monitoring.

## 1. Goal now
User goal: a **MoE inference-engine software factory**: input = model + system (host profile, memory budget) -> output = an engine (build + model representation + runtime flags) that uses **much less memory at about the same accuracy**. Load time, TTFT and tok/s may change (report them); KV-cache changes are allowed. Also in scope: (a) **Lab Manager design** (`MANAGER-DESIGN.md`, `LAB-FEASIBILITY.md`; deterministic coordination, our `bin/lab` is a TEMPORARY reference adapter, not the other team's lab agent), (b) the **CC portfolio** (`cc-inventory.csv`, builds/tools/methodologies with observed-vs-inferred status), (c) a **Friday 5-8 minute demo** (`cc/demo/DEMO.md`, `cc/demo/demo.sh`). Every result carries a claim category (computation-preserving engine gain | representation trade-off | runtime-placement trade-off | failed candidate | infrastructure/methodology | prediction) and a D012 transfer class (transferable | discrete-only | prediction). Proxies: Granite-3.1-1b-a400m (D001-D037; experts 0.84 MiB) and Qwen3-30B-A3B Q4_K_M (D038/D039; experts 2.72 MiB, does not fit the 16 GB GPU). Engine pin: llama.cpp `31288c9c6` (full `31288c9c66e59377f7788d920678a565bb89dd37`).

## 2. Lanes, hosts, branch
- Branch `x86/c2-resume` (HEAD bb6a65e at time of writing, 30 commits). `main` untouched. **Nothing pushed; pushing to `origin` (git@github.com:Muxite/siminfeng.git) is not authorized.**
- x86-main lane (this host): RTX 5070 Ti (discrete, sm_120), amd64, Docker (containerd store), one GPU job at a time by procedure only (no admission lock, D007). Models in `~/models/campaign/{gguf,qwen3-30b-a3b,data,tools}`; llama.cpp clone `ref/` and image archives are NOT in git.
- jetson-arm lane: separate host/lead. No SSH route. Exchange = operator-carried git bundle of `x86/c2-resume` (`git bundle verify` + sha256 in BUNDLE.sha256; ~68 MB history, no models/images/profiler reports) plus `handoff/jetson/EXCHANGE-1.md`. Jetson replies as `handoff/jetson/REPLY-1.md` + bundle of `jetson/<task>`. **No reply exists yet** (only EXCHANGE-1.md is in `handoff/jetson/`). Ownership: jetson owns `platform/jetson/**`, `cc/resource_observe/backends/jetson*`, `handoff/jetson/**` replies; x86 owns `cc/engine_handoff`, `cc/build_engine`, `bin/lab`, `cc/resource_observe/CONTRACT.md`.
- Working tree is dirty by design (many untracked `artifacts/codex*`; modified `evidence/claude-code.jsonl`, `artifacts/x2/loadmon.pid`, and `cc/routing_trace/routing-trace.patch` which T-QRT is editing). Do not `git add -A` blindly.

## 3. Results D020-D040 (verdict | category | numbers; all x86-main RTX 5070 Ti unless noted)

### D044 (E1): cache vs static on Qwen3-30B
Median decode t/s, chat/code:

| Budget | Static S2 | Cache C2 (share 0) | Cache C3 (share 0.9) | VRAM vs static |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 GB | 26.4/26.3 | 18.4/20.6 | 34.2/35.3 | |
| 6 GB | 31.4/28.9 | 32.2/34.0 | 48.4/48.1 | |
| 8 GB | 36.5/34.4 | 54.8/55.7 | 64.3/56.8 | |
| 10 GB | 43.8/43.3 | 71.9/71.1 | 71.9/64.2 | 3–6% less |

- C3 meets the speed rule at all four budgets; C1/C2 only at 8 and 10 GB.

## Adopted factory rules
1. Expert cache + CPU-share by default: share 0 if the predicted hit rate is ≥ about 90%, else 0.9.
2. ub trades TTFT against VRAM.
3. MTP n_max 3 when the model has MTP heads; n-gram for copy-heavy work.
4. Gate quality against the reference's batch-shape floor, never text identity.
5. Threads ≤ physical cores, autotuned; never SMT.
6. mmap; cold load = GB ÷ disk GB/s.
7. The quiet check should watch swap and page faults.

**Factory rules adopted (discrete GPU, measured on two models):**
1. Expert cache with CPU-share is the default placement. Share 0 if the predicted hit rate is ≥ about 90%, otherwise 0.9.
2. ub sets the TTFT vs VRAM trade: ub 1024–2048 removes the cache's TTFT penalty.
3. MTP n_max 3 when the model ships MTP heads. n-gram for copy-heavy workloads.
4. Gate quality with distributional checks against the reference's own batch-shape floor, never absolute text identity.
5. Threads ≤ physical cores, autotuned. Never SMT.
6. mmap. Budget cold load as GB ÷ disk GB/s.

## Findings to trust (with caveats in the D-notes)
1. Experts are 90.4% of weight bytes; mixed precision (experts Q4_K, rest Q8_0) halves Q4_K_M's quality loss at equal memory (D013).
2. Static layer offload (`--n-cpu-moe`) cuts GPU MiB linearly but decode collapses (discrete-only, D014). Page-cache-as-expert-cache has a sharp cliff when RAM < working set (D015, contaminated by concurrent compiles).
3. Granite routing skew is real vs a uniform control (D017), mild, weaker pooled across workloads.
4. Hybrid hit/miss dispatch is bitwise-exact; the serial cost model holds (33 us/miss); perfect-overlap upper bound NOT supported (D019).
5. Engine-native `--moe-cache-mib` (LRU, upload-on-miss) is slower than no cache until ~60% coverage (job-d50c052f94). The matched static-offload comparison in the same tool did not finish (D020) — rerun `lab/tests/static1.json`.

NO score
===== fail

Failure catalog 
 Failure Class Fix / rule 
 run_op left an orphan child when killed (D001) infra Process-group handling 
 reconcile overwrote a completed result (D006) infra Found by a recovery test 
 Build CC recorded the wrong image id (D016) identity Run by run_ref only 
 Lab crashed on non-UTF-8 output (D020) infra Bytes-safe capture 
 Static-hot never engaged (D024) engagement Engagement check before timing 
 PAP accepted from a download-contaminated window (D035 → D040) noise Quiet-host rerun rule 
 Codex brief refused by the provider (T-KVB) delegation Brief wording (linter gap) 
 CAL1 measured cache instead of DRAM measurement Rotating buffers and plausibility guards 
 CPU probe missing libcuda in a read-only container env Engine images need --gpus even for CPU 
 ngram made 0 drafts on Qwen engagement /no_think ; always log draft_n 
 pkill -f killed its own shell (twice) tooling Bracket trick; kill by PID 
 Overnight chain deadlocked 75 min on a stale self-matching waiter tooling Killed; same rule 
 CAL2 parser broke on the CUDA container banner fixtures Parse JSON lines only; capture real fixtures 
 KLD at batch 2048 could not see placement drift measurement Decode-path KLD at ub 1 (A2) 
 Absolute 97% gate failed by the reference itself gate design Gate against the batch-shape floor 
 Raw chat prompt ended at token 1 on Qwen3.6 engagement ChatML per model; check n > 0 
 Waiter fired on an old traceback in the log tooling Match only the completion marker 
 Swap episode slowed X8 2× (07:21–07:26) noise ABBA exposed it; rerun; add swap and page-fault watch to the quiet check 
 --no-mmap rejected by the new build env Use -lm none ; check rc per arm 
 User email in evidence files on a public repo privacy Scrubbed before push 

NO open
===== method

Methodologies 
Measurement 
Pre-register, then measure. Freeze the protocol before results exist. 
A/A first to get the noise floor, then matched A/B in ABBA order with medians. 
Quiet host: no compiles, Codex runs or unthrottled downloads. Check it per arm and label the arm otherwise. 
Rerun anything provisional that came from a noisy window. 
Profile with a perturbation check against unprofiled timing. 
Sample peak VRAM from outside the process (nvidia-smi every 0.5 s). 
Correctness 
Engagement before timing: prove the code path ran with counters or log lines. 
Text identity for exact rewrites. KLD/PPL for anything numerical, including placement. 
Paired KLD vs reference logits. Never unpaired PPL alone. 
test-backend-ops for every patched op. 
Sort every claim into a category: full-engine gain, representation trade-off, placement-only, or failed. 
Modeling and transfer 
Label each result transferable or proxy-only. Proxy results are hypotheses on the target. 
Predict from bytes and measured constants, and say "extrapolated" outside the calibration range. 
Report fixed per-layer cost next to per-byte cost. 
Plausibility guards on every microbenchmark (no faster-than-peak numbers). 
Leave one model out before trusting a fit. 
Process and delegation 
Opus orchestrates. Codex does bounded work from written assignments and is reviewed against real records. 
Capture real tool output as fixtures. Mocks hide real failures. 
Every action goes through run_op , so every number has a command. 
Research intake → smallest probe → indicative screen → frozen experiment → planner lever. 
Avoid pgrep / pkill patterns that can match their own command line. 

===== surpris

Expected vs unexpected 
Went as expected 
Decode is memory-bandwidth-bound wherever experts live. 
Quantization quality ordering: Q8 ≈ lossless, 4-bit costs a little, 2-bit collapses. 
CUDA graphs help (4.2%). Small-kernel fusion has headroom. 
KV q8_0 halves KV cost at no quality cost once fixed. 
Speculation gains depend on the workload. 
Surprised us 
The expert cache flipped from loser (Granite) to winner (Qwen), then won at 4 GB too once misses could stay on the CPU. 
Per-layer handoff, not bytes, dominated Granite decode (GPU idle 80%). 
3-bit experts were barely faster on the CPU. 
Qwen3 thinking mode silently disabled n-gram drafting. 
The handoff estimate varies 4× depending on the method (52–199 µs). 
Zen 2 exposes no DRAM counters to perf on this kernel. 
The same config gave different greedy text between runs. 
Provider refusals were triggered by crash/debug wording in a Codex brief. 
Rough base rates 
Of 23 written predictions: 8 confirmed, 4 magnitude off, 4 reversed, 7 silent failures. 
Anything that transfers from proxy to target: about half reversed or were off by more than 2×. 
First-run tooling on real output: about 1 in 2 needed a fix (CAL1, CAL2, T-CAL CPU probe, ngram, chain). 
Same-model, in-range predictions: almost always within 10%. 

===== correl

What correlates and what doesn't 
Strong, usable relationships 
 1/decode is linear in bytes moved off the GPU. On Qwen each CPU layer adds 0.757 ms, which is about 30 GB/s, and the line holds from K=8 to K=48 (D039). 
 VRAM is linear in K: about 347 MiB per Qwen layer and 27 MiB per Granite layer. Planner MiB error is under 0.3%. 
 Cache hit rate decides cache vs static. Upload-mode cache wins when held-out coverage is about 70% or higher. CPU-share removes most of the miss penalty, so it wins much lower. 
 Expert size × handoff cost decides granularity. Crossover = fixed cost / per-byte cost (D031). 
 Paired KLD tracks quality where unpaired PPL can't (stderr 0.0015 vs 0.37). 
 imatrix → lower KLD at every bit width (−33% at 4-bit, −13% at 3-bit). 
 Copy-heavy text → speculation acceptance. Rewrite and repeat prompts give 2.4–3×; chat gives none. 
 Prompt time falls roughly in proportion as ub rises (5.1 → 3.0 → 1.8 s), at about +0.3–0.5 GB per doubling. 
 The batch-shape floor is the same on both models (KLD 0.0058 vs 0.0059), so it can serve as a reusable quality yardstick. 
 Routing locality ranks code > prose > chat on both Granite and Qwen traces. 
Weak, misleading or absent 
 Fewer bits ≠ faster on CPU. Q3_K unpacking is compute-bound on AVX2, so 3-bit was only +1.5%. 
 Greedy text identity ≠ quality. Every placement changes the text. The same config can even change it between runs (62290c73 vs 77a3045a). 
 Harness speedups ≠ integrated speedups. The integrated graph pays per-layer fixed costs (D030). 
 Proxy-model results ≠ target results. Granite results flipped on Qwen twice (D022, the planner). 
 Kernel count ≠ bandwidth. 40–46% of kernel time is in tiny kernels at under 1% DRAM. 
 Cache-policy choice barely matters. LRU, SLRU and ClassLRU are within 2 points. Budget and miss handling matter far more. 
 Profiled time ≠ real time. Node tracing inflates gaps 3×, and ncu serialises kernels. 
 Identical bytes in a different file vary ±5%, so effects under 5% need A/A and alternation. 
 More threads ≠ faster: bandwidth saturates at 4 threads, and SMT halves decode. 
 CPU-share is not monotonic: a small share is worse than none or a large one. 
 Cache history changes both output and speed (chat 74 t/s fresh vs 57–66 after code prompts). 
 A reported hit rate can mislead (Strata: PCIe-served experts are not counted).

### Distinguishing the kinds of wins (do not mix these up)
- **Full-engine code gains (our code, computation-preserving):** only **q8_reuse, +2.1%** (Granite Q8_0, D029/D040).
  - `kv_quant_fix` is an engine **defect fix**. It enables q8_0 KV, which is a representation trade-off.
  - Neither was requalified on Qwen or on up1 for speed.
- **Upstream features used as levers (not our engineering), placement or runtime trade-offs:**
  - expert cache + CPU-share (D044, X3, X4);
  - ub (X6);
  - threads (X5);
  - mmap (X7).
- **Speculation, also upstream:** ngram (D045) and MTP (D046, X1, X8).
  - Text-identical on copy prompts.
  - Distributionally equivalent on chat (X2); text is not identical.
- **Representation trade-offs:**
  - mixE4K (D013);
  - imatrix (D035, accepted);
  - q8_0 KV (D033);
  - REAP pruning (E3; a model change with ×2.84 wikitext PPL);
  - PAP (rejected).
- **Component benchmarks:**
  - harness D019;
  - .so swap D036;
  - T-CAL2 (GPU 766, CPU 30.8, H2D 28.7 GB/s, handoff 52.5 µs residual);
  - bpftrace 0.79 ms per layer;
  - ncu 222 GB/s.
- **Simulations and predictions:** D014, planner (D034, D039), T-PL4, T-QRT, T-POL, T-SPECM. None of these is an engine result.
- **Headline memory result:** Qwen3-30B runs at 1.8 GB VRAM (vs 15.7 GB) with identical weights, 3.8× slower (D039). The cache + CPU-share + MTP stack then recovers +52% to +100% over static at about 8 GB (X8). **All of it is runtime configuration of upstream llama.cpp plus our release patches; the speed-ups are not our engine code.**

### 4d. Build and dependency problems
- **Image identity:** buildx under the containerd store reports the index digest as `.Id`. `docker run` rejects the bare config digest (exit 125). Rule: execute by run_ref, admit by config digest (D016, D023).
- **Build entitlements:** the b0 attempt 1 failed on bake fs entitlements.
- **Upstream drift:**
  - `--no-mmap` was replaced by `-lm none|mmap|mmap+mlock`.
  - The speculative flags changed (`--spec-type draft-mtp`, `--spec-draft-n-max`).
  - release-stack-1 needed a rebase to `3b4d6ab` (release-stack-2).
- **ABI:** the strict ABI diff says base → reuse libggml-cuda is INCOMPATIBLE (weak std::_Hashtable exports), yet the empirical swap works (D036). Keep both facts.
- **CPU probes in engine images need `--gpus`:** libcuda is linked even for CPU paths.
- **ccache:** patched rebuilds take about 10–20 s. A cold build takes minutes and pollutes timing windows.

### 4e. Permissions and settings needed
- **GPU sharing:** the owner's GPU services must be stopped by approval (D002) and restored afterwards.
- **Profiling:**
  - `perf_event_paranoid` lowered for perf and bpftrace (runtime, authorized);
  - ncu needs `--cap-add SYS_ADMIN` per container;
  - host `RmProfilingAdminOnly=1`.

### Distinguishing the kinds of wins (do not mix these up)
- **Full-engine code gains (our code, computation-preserving):** only **q8_reuse, +2.1%** (Granite Q8_0, D029/D040).
  - `kv_quant_fix` is an engine **defect fix**. It enables q8_0 KV, which is a representation trade-off.
  - Neither was requalified on Qwen or on up1 for speed.
- **Upstream features used as levers (not our engineering), placement or runtime trade-offs:**
  - expert cache + CPU-share (D044, X3, X4);
  - ub (X6);
  - threads (X5);
  - mmap (X7).
- **Speculation, also upstream:** ngram (D045) and MTP (D046, X1, X8).
  - Text-identical on copy prompts.
  - Distributionally equivalent on chat (X2); text is not identical.
- **Representation trade-offs:**
  - mixE4K (D013);
  - imatrix (D035, accepted);
  - q8_0 KV (D033);
  - REAP pruning (E3; a model change with ×2.84 wikitext PPL);
  - PAP (rejected).
- **Component benchmarks:**
  - harness D019;
  - .so swap D036;
  - T-CAL2 (GPU 766, CPU 30.8, H2D 28.7 GB/s, handoff 52.5 µs residual);
  - bpftrace 0.79 ms per layer;
  - ncu 222 GB/s.
- **Simulations and predictions:** D014, planner (D034, D039), T-PL4, T-QRT, T-POL, T-SPECM. None of these is an engine result.
- **Headline memory result:** Qwen3-30B runs at 1.8 GB VRAM (vs 15.7 GB) with identical weights, 3.8× slower (D039). The cache + CPU-share + MTP stack then recovers +52% to +100% over static at about 8 GB (X8). **All of it is runtime configuration of upstream llama.cpp plus our release patches; the speed-ups are not our engine code.**

### 4c. Repeated manual work (automation candidates)
- Restoring services and the GPU around timing windows (D002), done by hand every session.

### 4d. Build and dependency problems
- **Image identity:** buildx under the containerd store reports the index digest as `.Id`. `docker run` rejects the bare config digest (exit 125). Rule: execute by run_ref, admit by config digest (D016, D023).
- **Build entitlements:** the b0 attempt 1 failed on bake fs entitlements.
- **Upstream drift:**
  - `--no-mmap` was replaced by `-lm none|mmap|mmap+mlock`.
  - The speculative flags changed (`--spec-type draft-mtp`, `--spec-draft-n-max`).
  - release-stack-1 needed a rebase to `3b4d6ab` (release-stack-2).
- **ABI:** the strict ABI diff says base → reuse libggml-cuda is INCOMPATIBLE (weak std::_Hashtable exports), yet the empirical swap works (D036). Keep both facts.
- **CPU probes in engine images need `--gpus`:** libcuda is linked even for CPU paths.
- **ccache:** patched rebuilds take about 10–20 s. A cold build takes minutes and pollutes timing windows.

### 4e. Permissions and settings needed
- **GPU sharing:** the owner's GPU services must be stopped by approval (D002) and restored afterwards.
- **Profiling:**
  - `perf_event_paranoid` lowered for perf and bpftrace (runtime, authorized);
  - ncu needs `--cap-add SYS_ADMIN` per container;
  - host `RmProfilingAdminOnly=1`.
- **Push policy:** only the assigned branch; never `main`; no force-push; no permission-rule changes.
- **Container memory:** Qwen runs need a 40g container memory limit. Only one 18 GB-mmap process at a time on a 46 GB host.

### 4f. Platform, memory, profiling, sandbox, networking, scheduling, logging and recovery issues
- **Platform:**
  - PCIe-discrete results (layer-offload collapse, cache vs static) are labelled discrete-only (D012).
  - The Jetson lane found the upstream moe-cache **loses on UMA** (origin/jetson/c1 D030).
  - Never exchanged with x86: there is no SSH route, and the bundle has not been carried.
- **Memory:**
  - The gpu_budget shim is cooperative only; there is no hard VRAM cap (D021, D023).
  - About 310 MiB of VRAM is uncounted under NO_VMM.
  - Default-ctx KV (6144 MiB) dominates small budgets.
  - Host swap at 6.5 GB slowed runs by 2× (X8).
- **Profiling:**
  - Node tracing inflates gaps 3×; ncu serialises kernels.
  - CAL1 measured cache-resident bandwidth (1384 GB/s), so plausibility guards are now mandatory.
  - The handoff estimate varies 4× by method (52–199 µs).
- **Sandbox:**
  - Codex has no Docker or GPU, so all GPU work is the orchestrator's.
  - Codex's writes are confined to assignment roots, which the factory enforces.
  - The provider refused a debug-worded brief.
- **Networking:**
  - HF downloads run at about 1.4 MB/s (6 h for 22 GB).
  - The GitHub MCP server failed auth at closeout; plain git over SSH works.
- **Scheduling:**
  - One GPU job at a time by procedure, since there is no lock (D007).
  - Overnight chains are serial shell scripts with completion-marker waiters. Fragile: self-matching pgrep and old tracebacks firing a waiter early.
- **Logging:**
  - Raw evidence is verbose (`claude-code.jsonl` is 8 MB) and captured private data. Redaction is needed at capture.
  - `results.jsonl` is append-only per arm, which is good.
- **Recovery:**
  - A reconcile/overwrite bug (D006) and an orphan child (D001) were found by kill-per-phase tests.
  - A rerun is always a new attempt (att-N), never a relabel.
